claims.quote: there really can in some fundamental sense be an almost exponential difference in the amount of computational effort needed to find the behavior of a system with given particular initial conditions, and to solve the inverse problem of determining which if any initial conditions yield particular behavior.

claims.title: Computational irreducibility makes short theorems with only long proofs inevitable
claims.statement: Because the proof processes of almost every area of mathematics are computationally irreducible, adding axioms cannot remove the problem: there will essentially always be theorems that are short to state but whose shortest proofs are very long.
claims.author: Stephen Wolfram
claims.chapter: Ch. 12: The Principle of Computational Equivalence
claims.quote: But I suspect that ultimately there is almost always computational irreducibility, and this makes it essentially inevitable that there will be short theorems that only allow long proofs.

claims.title: An irreducible multiway system cannot be both complete and consistent
claims.statement: If questions about the long-run evolution of a multiway system (an idealized axiom system) are undecidable, then the system cannot be both complete and consistent, because completeness plus consistency would give a procedure that always terminates to decide whether a string is reached.
claims.author: Stephen Wolfram
claims.chapter: Ch. 12: The Principle of Computational Equivalence
claims.quote: So the result of this is that if the evolution of a multiway system is computationally irreducible—so that questions about its ultimate behavior are undecidable—the system cannot be both complete and consistent.

claims.title: Every axiom system used in current mathematical research is universal
claims.statement: Basic logic and pure predicate logic are not universal, but adding a function or relation with more than one argument gives universality; arithmetic, set theory, group theory and ring theory are universal, and every axiom system actually used in current mathematical research is known to be universal, while heavily constrained systems such as commutative group theory and simplified real algebra and geometry are not.
claims.author: Stephen Wolfram
claims.chapter: Ch. 12: The Principle of Computational Equivalence
claims.quote: But of the axiom systems actually used in current mathematics research every single one is now known to be universal.

claims.title: Beyond a low threshold almost every axiom system should be universal
claims.statement: The Principle of Computational Equivalence implies that, beyond a low threshold of complexity, almost any axiom system (including very simple ones) should be universal, and so should exhibit undecidability and have no general upper limit on proof length.
claims.author: Stephen Wolfram
claims.chapter: Ch. 12: The Principle of Computational Equivalence
claims.quote: And indeed the Principle of Computational Equivalence implies that beyond some low threshold almost any axiom system should be expected to be universal.

claims.title: Gödel's Theorem follows from the universality of arithmetic, shown via rule 110
claims.statement: An integer (exponential Diophantine) equation can be built whose solutions emulate the rule 110 cellular automaton; since rule 110 is universal, the axioms of arithmetic support universality, which implies Gödel's Theorem that arithmetic contains statements that cannot be proved true or false. Wolfram presents Gödel's Theorem as a consequence of the Principle of Computational Equivalence.
claims.author: Stephen Wolfram
claims.chapter: Ch. 12: The Principle of Computational Equivalence
claims.quote: And with the cellular automaton being a universal one such as rule 110 this implies that the axioms of arithmetic can support universality.

claims.title: Simple integer equations should exist whose lack of solutions is unprovable
claims.statement: Although known universal integer equations are very complicated (the simplest having 9 variables and an immense number of terms), there should be much simpler integer equations for which the absence of solutions can never be proved from the standard axioms of arithmetic.
claims.author: Stephen Wolfram
claims.chapter: Ch. 12: The Principle of Computational Equivalence
claims.quote: so that in fact there are in the end rather simple integer equations for which the absence of solutions can never be proved from the normal axioms of arithmetic.

claims.title: Many open number-theory problems may be unprovable from arithmetic's axioms
claims.statement: A fair fraction of the unsolved problems seriously studied in number theory will turn out to be questions that cannot be answered using the standard axioms of arithmetic.
claims.author: Stephen Wolfram
claims.chapter: Ch. 12: The Principle of Computational Equivalence
claims.quote: And it is my strong suspicion that in fact of all the current unsolved problems seriously studied in number theory a fair fraction will in the end turn out to be questions that cannot ever be answered using the normal axioms of arithmetic.

claims.title: Undecidability appears in almost any area of mathematics beyond easy questions
claims.statement: Undecidability and unprovability will begin to occur in practically any area of mathematics almost as soon as one goes beyond questions that are always easy to answer, as a consequence of the Principle of Computational Equivalence.
claims.author: Stephen Wolfram
claims.chapter: Ch. 12: The Principle of Computational Equivalence
claims.quote: And indeed from the Principle of Computational Equivalence I strongly believe that in general undecidability and unprovability will start to occur in practically any area of mathematics almost as soon as one goes beyond the level of questions that are always easy to answer.

claims.title: Mathematics avoids undecidability by choosing questions its methods can answer
claims.statement: Undecidability and unprovability have seemed rare in mathematics because mathematics, shaped by its history, has defined itself around the questions and systems that proof-based methods can address, concentrating on limited patches of computational reducibility; so present-day mathematics is a small and uncharacteristic sample of what is possible.
claims.author: Stephen Wolfram
claims.chapter: Ch. 12: The Principle of Computational Equivalence
claims.quote: it is that like most other fields of human inquiry mathematics has tended to define itself to be concerned with just those questions that its methods can successfully address.

claims.title: Complete and consistent means exactly half of all strings are generated
claims.statement: For a multiway system serving as an axiom system, with negation any length-preserving involution on strings, the system is complete and consistent exactly when half of all possible strings of each length are eventually generated from the string representing true; more than half implies inconsistency and less than half implies incompleteness.
claims.author: Stephen Wolfram
claims.chapter: Ch. 12: The Principle of Computational Equivalence
claims.quote: the criterion for whether a system is complete and consistent is simply that exactly half the possible strings of a given length are eventually generated if one starts from the string representing "true".

claims.title: Axiom systems used in mathematics are usually close to complete
claims.statement: The axiom systems widely used in mathematics, though usually incomplete, are typically close to complete, because they were built to describe definite kinds of objects; as a result, the alternative objects (nonstandard models) that also satisfy them, such as those for standard arithmetic, differ only in obscure ways.
claims.author: Stephen Wolfram
claims.chapter: Ch. 12: The Principle of Computational Equivalence
claims.quote: For if one looks at axiom systems that are widely used in mathematics they almost all tend to be complete enough to prove at least a fair fraction of statements either true or false.

claims.title: Most simple axiom systems admit many different operator forms
claims.statement: Enumerating simple axiom systems for a binary operator shows that the vast majority allow operators of many different forms (many models), so they are not about any one particular operator and are far from complete; only a few, such as those for logic, force essentially a single form.
claims.author: Stephen Wolfram
claims.chapter: Ch. 12: The Principle of Computational Equivalence
claims.quote: But what the pictures on the next two pages [804, 805] show is that the vast majority of axiom systems actually allow operators with all sorts of different forms.

claims.title: Very short single-axiom systems for logic exist among the simplest axiom systems
claims.statement: Propositional logic can be axiomatized in terms of Nand by a single axiom with only six Nands (found by searching small axiom systems), far shorter than textbook systems, so an axiom system for logic is likely to be found among the simplest few thousand axiom systems.
claims.author: Stephen Wolfram
claims.chapter: Ch. 12: The Principle of Computational Equivalence
claims.quote: So what this means is that if one were just to go through a list of the simplest few thousand axiom systems one would already be quite likely to find one that represents logic.

claims.title: Traditional axiom systems are not fundamentally special; others could found new fields
claims.statement: Apart from history, nothing fundamentally distinguishes the axiom systems traditionally used in mathematics (logic included), and many other axiom systems, often simple ones, could serve as foundations for new fields of mathematics as rich as the traditional ones.
claims.author: Stephen Wolfram
claims.chapter: Ch. 12: The Principle of Computational Equivalence
claims.quote: So this leads to the conclusion that there is in a sense nothing fundamentally special about the particular axiom systems that have traditionally been used in mathematics

claims.title: Named textbook theorems of logic are those not derivable from simpler ones
claims.statement: If the theorems of basic logic are listed in order of increasing complexity, the ones that cannot be derived from simpler theorems earlier in the list are almost exactly the ones traditional textbooks single out and name as interesting.
claims.author: Stephen Wolfram
claims.chapter: Ch. 12: The Principle of Computational Equivalence
claims.quote: And remarkably enough what I have found is that these theorems are almost exactly the ones highlighted on the previous page that have traditionally been identified as interesting.

claims.title: Judgments like deep or powerful reflect the structure of the theorem network
claims.statement: Mathematicians' intuitive descriptions of theorems (difficult, powerful, surprising, deep) reflect features of the network of statements connected by theorems, and fields regarded as more successful should have more compact networks while fields full of isolated facts, such as elementary number theory, should have sparser networks.
claims.author: Stephen Wolfram
claims.chapter: Ch. 12: The Principle of Computational Equivalence
claims.quote: And my suspicion is that our intuitive characterizations of theorems are in effect just reflections of our perception of various features of the structure of this network.

claims.title: No general definition of intelligence independent of human details
claims.statement: General features proposed as marks of intelligence (learning and memory, adaptation, abstraction) occur in systems such as simple cellular automata and fluids, so there is no workable general definition of intelligence; any usable one must be tied to specific details of human intelligence.
claims.author: Stephen Wolfram
claims.chapter: Ch. 12: The Principle of Computational Equivalence
claims.quote: My guess is that ultimately there is not, and that in fact any workable definition of what we normally think of as intelligence will end up having to be tied to all sorts of seemingly rather specific details of human intelligence.

claims.title: Proposed general features of life occur in many simple-rule systems
claims.statement: Almost any general feature proposed to characterize life, including self-organization, self-reproduction and complexity, occurs even in many systems with very simple rules, so life can only be recognized by specific shared details with life on Earth.
claims.author: Stephen Wolfram
claims.chapter: Ch. 12: The Principle of Computational Equivalence
claims.quote: Indeed, following the discoveries in this book I have come to the conclusion that almost any general feature that one might think of as characterizing life will actually occur even in many systems with very simple rules.

claims.title: Human artifacts look simple because engineering requires predictability
claims.statement: Human-made artifacts tend to look simpler than natural objects because engineers need to foresee what their systems will do, which requires computational reducibility, whereas nature has no such constraint and many natural systems are computationally irreducible.
claims.author: Stephen Wolfram
claims.chapter: Ch. 12: The Principle of Computational Equivalence
claims.quote: And I believe the basic answer to this has to do with the fact that when we as humans set up artifacts we usually need to be able to foresee what they will do—for otherwise we have no way to tell whether they will achieve the purposes we want.

claims.title: A minimal rule for a feature hints that a system was made for a purpose
claims.statement: Since purposes can always be reinterpreted as mechanisms, purpose cannot be identified for certain from behavior; the best criterion is that a system is the minimal or optimal one producing a given feature, which suggests it was built for that purpose, as advanced technology should increasingly use minimal systems.
claims.author: Stephen Wolfram
claims.chapter: Ch. 12: The Principle of Computational Equivalence
claims.quote: finding out that the rule for the system is the minimal or optimal one for producing that feature may make it seem more likely that at least with sufficiently advanced technology the system might have specifically been created for the purpose of exhibiting that feature.

claims.title: Efficient extraterrestrial communications would show no detectable regularities
claims.statement: Signals used for communication by an advanced extraterrestrial civilization would likely be compressed to the point of showing essentially no detectable regularities, so they would look like random radio noise, and searches for sharply defined carrier frequencies would miss them; only beacons meant to be noticed would need recognizable regularities.
claims.author: Stephen Wolfram
claims.chapter: Ch. 12: The Principle of Computational Equivalence
claims.quote: my guess is that they will exhibit essentially no detectable regularities. For any such regularity represents in a sense a redundancy or inefficiency that can be removed by the sender and receiver both using appropriate data compression.

claims.title: Sophisticated computation, or primes, are not signs of intelligence
claims.statement: Producing a signal by sophisticated computation is no evidence of intelligence, because such computation is common in ordinary physical processes; for instance, turbulence in the gas around a star quickly does more computation than all of human intellectual history, and sequences such as the primes can be generated by many non-intelligent systems.
claims.author: Stephen Wolfram
claims.chapter: Ch. 12: The Principle of Computational Equivalence
claims.quote: And indeed it seems likely that for example an ordinary physical process like fluid turbulence in the gas around a star should rather quickly do more computation than has by most measures ever been done throughout the whole course of human intellectual history.

claims.title: Recognizing extraterrestrial intelligence depends on similarity to humans
claims.statement: The difficulty in finding extraterrestrial intelligence is not finding systems that compute in sophisticated ways, which are common, but finding ones whose details are similar enough to humans that we would recognize them as intelligent; somewhat generalized intelligence is likely to exist but to behave in bizarrely unhuman ways.
claims.author: Stephen Wolfram
claims.chapter: Ch. 12: The Principle of Computational Equivalence
claims.quote: that the basic issue is not finding systems that perform sophisticated enough computations, but rather finding ones whose details happen to be similar enough to us as humans that we recognize what they do as showing intelligence.

claims.title: Engineering has explored only a tiny unrepresentative fraction of possible systems
claims.statement: Traditional engineering has used only a tiny and unrepresentative fraction of possible systems and processes, those simple enough to predict, and using simple-rule systems with complex behavior will make a vast amount of new technology possible.
claims.author: Stephen Wolfram
claims.chapter: Ch. 12: The Principle of Computational Equivalence
claims.quote: And indeed one of the things that emerges from this book is that traditional engineering has actually considered only a tiny and quite unrepresentative fraction of all the kinds of systems and processes that are in principle possible.

claims.title: Simple universal rules like rule 110 could be built into computers from atoms
claims.statement: Since very simple rules such as the rule 110 cellular automaton are universal, computers could be built from many kinds of components, and a simple chemical process could plausibly assemble a rule 110-like computer at the atomic scale, with one or a few atoms per cell.
claims.author: Stephen Wolfram
claims.chapter: Ch. 12: The Principle of Computational Equivalence
claims.quote: For while it is quite implausible that some simple chemical process could successfully assemble a traditional computer out of atoms, it seems quite plausible that this could be done for something like a rule 110 cellular automaton.

claims.title: Exhaustive search is the only reliable way to find programs with given behavior
claims.statement: Because simple programs can do so many unexpected things, and computational irreducibility can make finding a behavior take irreducible work, the only reliable way to find a simple program with a desired behavior is essentially exhaustive search, so building a library of basic knowledge about simple programs is a better route to technology.
claims.author: Stephen Wolfram
claims.chapter: Ch. 12: The Principle of Computational Equivalence
claims.quote: ultimately the only way to find what one wants is essentially just to do an exhaustive search of all possibilities.

claims.title: Humans are not computationally more sophisticated than other systems in nature
claims.statement: By the Principle of Computational Equivalence, human brains, turbulent fluids, simple cellular automata and the universe as a whole all achieve the same level of computational sophistication, so humans are not fundamentally special in intelligence or complexity.
claims.author: Stephen Wolfram
claims.chapter: Ch. 12: The Principle of Computational Equivalence
claims.quote: So this means that there is in the end no difference between the level of computational sophistication that is achieved by humans and by all sorts of other systems in nature and elsewhere.

claims.title: Computational irreducibility puts permanent limits on scientific prediction
claims.statement: The Principle of Computational Equivalence and computational irreducibility show that science will never predict everything: even if the universe follows simple rules, there is in general no way to know all their consequences except by watching them unfold.
claims.author: Stephen Wolfram
claims.chapter: Ch. 12: The Principle of Computational Equivalence
claims.quote: But the Principle of Computational Equivalence—and the phenomenon of computational irreducibility—now shows that this will never happen.

claims.title: Self-assembly emerges from cells sharing a common model of organismal form
claims.statement: In simulations based on variational free-energy minimization (active inference), cells that share a common genetically and epigenetically specified model of the organism's form self-assemble into that form, offering a proof of principle that self-assembly can be an emergent property of such cells.
claims.author: Michael Levin
claims.work: Knowing one's place: a free-energy approach to pattern regulation
claims.chapter: Friston K 2015, Knowing one's place: a free-energy approach to pattern regulation › Abstract
claims.quote: Here, we offer a proof of principle that self-assembly is an emergent property of cells that share a common (genetic and epigenetic) model of organismal form.

claims.title: Genome parametrizes a generative model; epigenesis inverts it
claims.statement: Under the free-energy account of morphogenesis, genetic codes can be interpreted as parametrizing a generative model that predicts the signals each cell would sense in the target morphology, and epigenetic processes (signalling-dependent transcription) as the inversion of that model.
claims.author: Michael Levin
claims.work: Knowing one's place: a free-energy approach to pattern regulation
claims.chapter: Friston K 2015, Knowing one's place: a free-energy approach to pattern regulation › Abstract
claims.quote: This novel perspective on the coordination of migration and differentiation of cells suggests an interpretation of genetic codes as parametrizing a generative model—predicting the signals sensed by cells in the target morphology—and epigenetic processes as the subsequent inversion of that model.

claims.title: Morphogenesis requires each cell to model its place in the target form
claims.statement: Friston, Levin, Sengupta and Pezzulo propose that morphogenetic self-organization requires each cell to have an implicit model of its place in the final morphology, with self-assembly being cells moving to sample the local signals that model predicts (minimizing variational free energy).
claims.author: Michael Levin
claims.work: Knowing one's place: a free-energy approach to pattern regulation
claims.chapter: Friston K 2015, Knowing one's place: a free-energy approach to pattern regulation › Introduction
claims.quote: In this paper, we pursue the notion that morphogenetic self-organization requires each cell to have an implicit model of its place in the final morphology [21]—and that self-assembly is the process of moving to sample local signals that are predicted by that model.

claims.title: Free energy is minimized only when every cell occupies a unique inferred place
claims.statement: In the active-inference model of morphogenesis, where identical pluripotent cells share one generative model, the minimum of variational free energy is reached only when every cell is at a unique location and has correctly inferred its place, so free-energy minimization guarantees convergence to the target form.
claims.author: Michael Levin
claims.work: Knowing one's place: a free-energy approach to pattern regulation
claims.chapter: Friston K 2015, Knowing one's place: a free-energy approach to pattern regulation › Introduction
claims.quote: This is guaranteed because the minimum of variational free energy is obtained when each cell is in a unique location and has correctly inferred its place.

claims.title: Simulated cells resolve fate ambiguity using context set by other ambiguous cells
claims.statement: In the active-inference simulation, identical undifferentiated cells starting at one location migrate rapidly to their target locations and then differentiate (around the eighth time step) into head, body and tail types as ensemble free energy falls, showing cells can resolve ambiguity about their fate even when it depends on context set by other equally ambiguous cells.
claims.author: Michael Levin
claims.work: Knowing one's place: a free-energy approach to pattern regulation
claims.chapter: Friston K 2015, Knowing one's place: a free-energy approach to pattern regulation › Simulating self-assembly
claims.quote: These results are compelling in the sense that they show cells can resolve ambiguity about their fate, even when that resolution depends upon the context established by other (equally ambiguous) cells.

claims.title: Bisected simulated embryos regenerate the full target form
claims.statement: When the partially differentiated simulated embryo is cut in two and each half's cells are replicated, the cells undergo slight dedifferentiation and then each half regenerates the complete head–body–tail target morphology, illustrating pluripotency and recovery from drastic interventions in the active-inference model.
claims.author: Michael Levin
claims.work: Knowing one's place: a free-energy approach to pattern regulation
claims.chapter: Friston K 2015, Knowing one's place: a free-energy approach to pattern regulation › Simulating regeneration and dysmorphogenesis
claims.quote: This example illustrates the pluripotential nature of the cells and the ability of self-assembly to recover from fairly drastic interventions.

claims.title: Altering signal sensitivity without changing the model predicts specific birth defects
claims.statement: In the active-inference morphogenesis model, changing cells' sensitivity to extracellular, exogenous or intracellular signals without changing the generative model produces specific dysmorphogenesis, e.g. reducing sensitivity to the head-expressed signal shrinks the head, and doubling sensitivity to intracellular signals causes failed migration, differentiation and atrophy; these are predictions for pharmacological manipulation of intercellular signalling.
claims.author: Michael Levin
claims.work: Knowing one's place: a free-energy approach to pattern regulation
claims.chapter: Friston K 2015, Knowing one's place: a free-energy approach to pattern regulation › Simulating regeneration and dysmorphogenesis
claims.quote: More selective interventions produce a dysmorphogenesis of various segments of the target morphology: reducing sensitivity to the second chemotactic signal—that is expressed by head cells—reduces the size of the head.

claims.title: Neural and bioelectric patterning networks may share dynamics
claims.statement: Because non-neuronal cells use many of the same ion-channel and electrical-synapse mechanisms as neurons for pattern formation and repair, significant commonalities may exist between the dynamics of neural networks and of bioelectric signalling networks that control shape, so neural modelling tools such as dynamic causal modelling may apply to morphogenesis data.
claims.author: Michael Levin
claims.work: Knowing one's place: a free-energy approach to pattern regulation
claims.chapter: Friston K 2015, Knowing one's place: a free-energy approach to pattern regulation › Conclusion
claims.quote: This suggests the possibility that significant commonalities may exist between the dynamics of neural networks and of bioelectric signalling networks that control shape determination [20,21,83].

claims.title: An exogenous gradient makes self-assembly more robust for larger ensembles
claims.statement: In the active-inference morphogenesis simulations, an exogenous concentration gradient is not necessary but yields a more robust solution for larger ensembles (more than four clones) and fixes the orientation of the target morphology relative to an external frame of reference.
claims.author: Michael Levin
claims.work: Knowing one's place: a free-energy approach to pattern regulation
claims.chapter: Friston K 2015, Knowing one's place: a free-energy approach to pattern regulation › Conclusion
claims.quote: This is not a necessary component of the scheme; however, our simulations suggest that it underwrites a more robust solution for larger ensembles (with more than four clones).

claims.title: Epigenetic active inference is indispensable for patterning beyond genetic encoding
claims.statement: Although aspects of the target morphology are genetically encoded in the parameters of cells' generative models, epigenetic processes (active inference) are indispensable for patterning, consistent with the regenerative target morphology of planaria being permanently alterable (to two heads) by a brief modification of electric synapses.
claims.author: Michael Levin
claims.work: Knowing one's place: a free-energy approach to pattern regulation
claims.chapter: Friston K 2015, Knowing one's place: a free-energy approach to pattern regulation › Conclusion
claims.quote: It may be worth concluding that although aspects of the target morphology are genetically encoded (in the parameters of the generative models); epigenetic processes (active inference) are indispensable for patterning.

claims.title: Brief gap-junction blockade makes G. dorotocephala regenerate other species' head shapes
claims.statement: In decapitated Girardia dorotocephala fragments, a transient perturbation of cell-to-cell physiological connectivity with the gap junction blocker octanol can lead to regenerated heads whose shapes stochastically match those of other planarian species (Schmidtea mediterranea, Dugesia japonica, Polycelis felina).
claims.author: Michael Levin
claims.work: Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms
claims.chapter: Emmons-Bell M 2015, Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms › Abstract
claims.quote: after decapitation in G. dorotocephala, a transient perturbation of physiological connectivity among cells (using the gap junction blocker octanol) can result in regenerated heads with quite different shapes, stochastically matching other known species of planaria (S. mediterranea, D. japonica, and P. felina)

claims.title: Octanol-induced head shapes are morphometrically closer to the species they resemble
claims.statement: By geometric morphometrics (Procrustes distances), the octanol-induced head shapes of G. dorotocephala regenerates are closer to the wild-type head shapes of the species they resemble than to the wild-type G. dorotocephala head shape.
claims.author: Michael Levin
claims.work: Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms
claims.chapter: Emmons-Bell M 2015, Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms › 2. Results › 2.2. Quantitative Comparison of Induced vs. Genome-Specific Head Shapes
claims.quote: Comparisons of the Procrustes distances between shape groups (Figure 2A, Table 1) showed that the experimentally derived morphologies were closer in shape to the wild-type morphologies they resembled than the wild-type Girardia dorotocephala head morphology.

claims.title: Induced head shapes are stochastic, with frequencies tracking evolutionary distance
claims.statement: Under identical octanol treatment, G. dorotocephala regenerates take one of several discrete head shapes, and the frequencies of the shapes are unequal and correlate roughly with the evolutionary distance (from rRNA phylogeny) between G. dorotocephala and the species each shape resembles, with shapes of closer relatives (S. mediterranea, D. japonica) more frequent than that of the more distant P. felina.
claims.author: Michael Levin
claims.work: Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms
claims.chapter: Emmons-Bell M 2015, Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms › 2. Results › 2.3. The Head Shape Changes Are Stochastic
claims.quote: We conclude that not only are phenotypic outcomes from physiological network perturbation stochastic (as the same treatment leads to one of several discrete shapes among individuals), but the frequencies are not equal and correlate roughly with evolutionary distance between the worm species these heads resemble.

claims.title: Gap-junction-perturbed worms also acquire the brain shape of the species they resemble
claims.statement: G. dorotocephala regenerates whose heads resemble another species after octanol treatment also have brain morphologies (length/width ratio, by anti-synapsin staining) resembling the brains of wild-type worms of that species.
claims.author: Michael Levin
claims.work: Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms
claims.chapter: Emmons-Bell M 2015, Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms › 2. Results › 2.4. Brain Structure of GJ-Perturbed Worms Is Also Altered to That of Other Species
claims.quote: Strikingly, we found that pseudo worms possessed brain morphologies that look like the brain morphologies of wild-type worms whose head shapes they resembled (Figure 4D–F) (ANOVA, p < 0.001).

claims.title: Perturbed worms adopt the anterior stem-cell distribution of the species they resemble
claims.statement: In octanol-treated G. dorotocephala regenerates, the transformation toward another species' head shape extends to the species-characteristic distribution of neoblasts (mitotic stem cells) in the anterior body, and the authors conclude that the patterning processes disrupted by gap junction perturbation also organize the distribution of mitotically active cells.
claims.author: Michael Levin
claims.work: Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms
claims.chapter: Emmons-Bell M 2015, Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms › 2. Results › 2.5. Distribution of Neoblasts Is Altered to That of Other Species in GJ-Perturbed Worms
claims.quote: We conclude that the transformation of G. dorotocephala worms to resemble other species also extends to the species-specific, characteristic internal distribution of their stem cells, and that the patterning processes that are disrupted after GJC perturbation are also responsible for organizing the distribution of mitotically active cells.

claims.title: Octanol-treated worms show more isopotential regions, which return to normal by 30 days
claims.statement: Ten days after transient octanol exposure, regenerated G. dorotocephala show more distinct isopotential (membrane-voltage) regions by DiBAC dye imaging than controls, and the number of isopotential regions returns to the wild-type level after 30 days of morphological remodeling.
claims.author: Michael Levin
claims.work: Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms
claims.chapter: Emmons-Bell M 2015, Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms › 2. Results › 2.6. Patterns of Endogenous Relative Membrane Potential Are Altered in GJ-Perturbed Worms
claims.quote: We detected an increased number of isopotential regions in the pseudo worms compared to the states of control worms; interestingly, the numbers of isopotential regions return to those of a wild-type state after 30 days of morphological remodeling (Figure 6I).

claims.title: Induced head shapes remodel back toward G. dorotocephala after regeneration ends
claims.statement: The other-species head shapes induced in G. dorotocephala by octanol are not permanent: between days 10 and 30, after regeneration is complete and without further injury, the heads are remodeled to more closely resemble wild-type G. dorotocephala.
claims.author: Michael Levin
claims.work: Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms
claims.chapter: Emmons-Bell M 2015, Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms › 2. Results › 2.7. Induced Shape Changes Are Not Permanent
claims.quote: We found that the induced morphologies were remodeled, long after regenerative processes had ended, to produce morphologies that bore closer resemblance to wild-type G. dorotocephala.

claims.title: Head remodeling passes from S. mediterranea-like to D. japonica-like to normal shape
claims.statement: In canonical variate shape space, the D. japonica head morphology lies between those of G. dorotocephala and S. mediterranea, and octanol-induced S. mediterranea-like G. dorotocephala heads remodel by moving from S. mediterranea-like to D. japonica-like to G. dorotocephala morphology.
claims.author: Michael Levin
claims.work: Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms
claims.chapter: Emmons-Bell M 2015, Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms › 2. Results › 2.7. Induced Shape Changes Are Not Permanent
claims.quote: DJ morphology lies between GD and SM morphologies in this space, and we observe remodeling that moves from SM morphology to DJ morphology to GD morphology.

claims.title: Agent-based model of migrating, signaling cells reproduces the observed head shapes
claims.statement: In an agent-based model of planarian head regeneration in which static somatic cells emit a chemical signal and migratory cells (neoblasts or their progeny) are repelled by it, deactivating different subsets of signaling cells (representing octanol gap-junction blockade) reproduces the four observed head shapes, so a small set of gap-junction-regulated cell behaviors such as migration and cell-cell signaling can quantitatively explain the observed morphologies.
claims.author: Michael Levin
claims.work: Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms
claims.chapter: Emmons-Bell M 2015, Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms › 2. Results › 2.8. A Model of Planarian Head Shapes Arising from Cell Interactions
claims.quote: We conclude that a small set of cell-level behaviors, such as migration and cell-cell signaling that are known to be regulated by GJC and thus are perturbed by octanol exposure [35,39,49,98,101,102], can quantitatively explain the morphologies we observed in planaria.

claims.title: Coherent discrete head shapes show the octanol effect is instructive rather than toxic
claims.statement: The octanol-induced head-shape change in G. dorotocephala is instructive rather than a toxic or housekeeping defect, because it yields one of several coherent, ecologically valid morphologies rather than regeneration failure or disorganized growth, with no intermediate morphologies observed.
claims.author: Michael Levin
claims.work: Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms
claims.chapter: Emmons-Bell M 2015, Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms › 3. Discussion › 3.1. Perturbation of Bioelectric Networks Produces Inter-Species Morphological Change
claims.quote: The head morphology alteration effect was instructive, and not merely one of toxicity or a house-keeping defect, because the outcome was not merely disruption of regenerative ability or a generalized mis-patterning (e.g., tumor or other disorganized growth), but rather resulted in one of several coherent (and ecologically-valid) morphologies.

claims.title: Hexanol, which does not block gap junctions, does not alter head shape
claims.statement: In G. dorotocephala, the same 3-day exposure to hexanol, a closely related alcohol that does not efficiently block gap junction channels, does not produce altered head morphologies, consistent with the head-shape change depending on octanol's gap-junction-blocking activity rather than a generalized effect of long-chain alcohols.
claims.author: Michael Levin
claims.work: Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms
claims.chapter: Emmons-Bell M 2015, Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms › 3. Discussion › 3.1. Perturbation of Bioelectric Networks Produces Inter-Species Morphological Change
claims.quote: The same 3-day treatment with the closely related alcohol, hexanol (6-OH), which does not efficiently block gap junction channels, and subsequent regeneration in water for 7 days, did not produce altered morphologies, consistent with the importance of the GJ-blocking activity of octanol, and not some other generalized effect of long-chain alcohols.

claims.title: Bioelectric networks derive distinct morphologies from one genome
claims.statement: Physiological bioelectric networks are a previously unrecognized input by which distinct morphologies, including those of other species, can be derived from the same genome, as shown by gap-junction perturbation in G. dorotocephala.
claims.author: Michael Levin
claims.work: Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms
claims.chapter: Emmons-Bell M 2015, Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms › 3. Discussion › 3.1. Perturbation of Bioelectric Networks Produces Inter-Species Morphological Change
claims.quote: Here, we identify a novel physiological input into the process by which distinct morphologies can be derived from the same genome: physiological bioelectric networks.

claims.title: Brief gap-junction blockade persistently alters bioelectric state after drug washout
claims.statement: In G. dorotocephala, the long-lasting alteration of bioelectric patterning after brief octanol exposure is not caused by residual octanol (which leaves tissues within 24 h) but is initiated by octanol's disruption of gap junction communication, which alters bioelectric network topology and results in a persistent perturbation of bioelectric state.
claims.author: Michael Levin
claims.work: Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms
claims.chapter: Emmons-Bell M 2015, Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms › 3. Discussion › 3.4. Bioelectric State of Tissues and Its Stable Alteration in Species-Specific Shape Change
claims.quote: Although these long-lasting alterations in bioelectrical patterning are not directly caused by octanol remaining within the body of the worm (since 8-OH is known to depart planarian tissues within 24 h [20]), they are initiated by the octanol-mediated disruption of GJC, which alters bioelectric network topology, and results in persistent perturbation of bioelectric state.

claims.title: Partial, variable gap-junction blockade is consistent with stochastic head-shape outcomes
claims.statement: The variability and overall magnitude of the bioelectric effect imply that octanol only partially shuts down gap junction communication in each G. dorotocephala (affecting some percentage of gap junctions per animal), which the authors consider consistent with the stochasticity of the head-shape phenotype.
claims.author: Michael Levin
claims.work: Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms
claims.chapter: Emmons-Bell M 2015, Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms › 3. Discussion › 3.4. Bioelectric State of Tissues and Its Stable Alteration in Species-Specific Shape Change
claims.quote: The variability and overall magnitude of the effect imply that the result of 8-OH exposure is only partially effective in shutting down GJC (affecting some percentage of GJs in any animal); this is consistent with the stochasticity of the morphological phenotype (Figure 3).

claims.title: Head shape may be encoded in time-dependent rather than steady voltage patterns
claims.statement: Because single-image voltage distributions showed no simple correspondence with the head shapes of octanol-treated G. dorotocephala, the authors consider it most likely that shape outcomes are encoded in time-dependent bioelectric activity rather than in steady voltage distributions, as in information encoding in the central nervous system.
claims.author: Michael Levin
claims.work: Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms
claims.chapter: Emmons-Bell M 2015, Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms › 3. Discussion › 3.4. Bioelectric State of Tissues and Its Stable Alteration in Species-Specific Shape Change
claims.quote: The most likely explanation however is that shape outcomes may not be encoded via steady (single-image) distributions but in time-dependent activity, as occurs during information encoding in the central nervous system.

claims.title: Planarian morphology behaves as a homeostatic parameter maintained toward a target shape
claims.statement: In planarians, morphology appears to be a homeostatic parameter that is repeatedly assessed and adjusted to maintain a 'target' morphology: after an incorrect head shape is produced during regeneration, the mismatch with the target triggers remodeling (between days 10 and 17 in octanol-treated G. dorotocephala), even after large-scale reorganization has ended.
claims.author: Michael Levin
claims.work: Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms
claims.chapter: Emmons-Bell M 2015, Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms › 3. Discussion › 3.5. Morphological Remodeling in 2 Phases: Head Shape Change without Traumatic Injury
claims.quote: Morphology appears to be a homeostatic parameter, one that is consistently assessed and adjusted in order to maintain some “target” morphology.

claims.title: Gap-junction-dependent instructive signals pass from somatic tissue to neoblasts
claims.statement: The authors propose that significant instructive, gap-junction-dependent signaling passes from planarian somatic tissues to neoblasts or their progeny to guide new tissue generation and shaping during regeneration.
claims.author: Michael Levin
claims.work: Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms
claims.chapter: Emmons-Bell M 2015, Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms › 3. Discussion › 3.6. Computational Modeling of Head Shape Formation
claims.quote: In this model, we propose that significant instructive (GJ-dependent) signaling occurs from the somatic tissues to the neoblasts or their progeny, to guide the new tissue generation and shaping during regeneration.

claims.title: Somatic cells can be modeled as a slow neural-like network obeying brain-like dynamics
claims.statement: The authors propose conceptualizing the link between gap junctional connectivity among planarian cells and discrete regenerative outcomes by viewing the cells as a neural-like network that processes developmental information more slowly but obeys the same statistical dynamics as the brain.
claims.author: Michael Levin
claims.work: Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms
claims.chapter: Emmons-Bell M 2015, Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms › 3. Discussion › 3.7. A hypothesis: Physiological Network Attractors Underlie Regions of Anatomical Morphospace
claims.quote: Thus, we propose that one way to conceptualize the linkage between bioelectrical connectivity among worm cells (GJC) and discrete global behavioral outcomes achieved by regeneration is to view the worms’ cells as a neural-like network, processing developmental information more slowly but obeying the same statistical dynamics rules as are known to occur in the brain (Figure 9A).

claims.title: Planarian head shapes may be attractors of a gap-junction-coupled bioelectric network
claims.statement: The authors hypothesize that distinct planarian head shapes may be attractors in the state space of the bioelectric network formed by body cells coupled by gap junctions, that these attractors correspond to regions of morphospace in the evolutionary sense, and that octanol knocks the network's stochastic dynamics into one of several nearby attractors normally belonging to other flatworm species.
claims.author: Michael Levin
claims.work: Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms
claims.chapter: Emmons-Bell M 2015, Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms › 3. Discussion › 3.7. A hypothesis: Physiological Network Attractors Underlie Regions of Anatomical Morphospace
claims.quote: We hypothesize that distinct shape outcomes may be attractors in a state space describing distinct modes of the bioelectric network of planarian body cells connected by gap junctions (electrical synapses); in essence, these attractors correspond to regions of a morphospace as classically understood by evolutionary theory [151].

claims.title: Regeneration as descent to a free-energy attractor; induced shapes as local minima
claims.statement: On the authors' proposed view, discrete planarian head patterns are the lowest free-energy outcomes of bioelectric network dynamics; amputation raises free energy and regeneration is a return to a low-energy attractor, octanol shifts the system to another attractor, and the induced other-species shapes are only local minima since worms return to the global minimum of G. dorotocephala morphology after about 3–4 weeks.
claims.author: Michael Levin
claims.work: Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms
claims.chapter: Emmons-Bell M 2015, Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms › 3. Discussion › 3.7. A hypothesis: Physiological Network Attractors Underlie Regions of Anatomical Morphospace
claims.quote: On this view (Figure 9), the discrete head patterns are outcomes of bioelectric network dynamics with the lowest free-energy; cutting the network raises the free energy by deviating the system from its optimal morphology (damage), and initiates the regenerative process—a journey back down to a low-energy attractor.

claims.title: Planarian evolutionary distance may reflect ease of shifting a shared patterning network
claims.statement: The authors suggest that a core network of gene-regulatory elements and gap-junction-mediated signals may be shared among many planarians, with species differences tweaking its dynamics, so that evolutionary distance between planarian species may reflect how easily this network can be shifted into its different outcome states, as during gap junction inhibition.
claims.author: Michael Levin
claims.work: Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms
claims.chapter: Emmons-Bell M 2015, Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms › 3. Discussion › 3.8. Stochastic Phenotypes and Evolutionary Implications
claims.quote: The evolutionary distance among the planarian types may thus be expected to reflect the ease of shifting this network into its different potential outcome states (as occurs during GJC inhibition).

claims.title: Resting potential of distant cells controls oncogene-dependent tumorigenesis
claims.statement: The resting membrane potentials of cells located at a distance from oncogene-expressing cells are critical for whether those oncogene-expressing cells go on to form tumors in vivo, as shown in Xenopus laevis tadpoles injected with human oncogenes.
claims.author: Michael Levin
claims.work: Transmembrane voltage potential of somatic cells controls oncogene-mediated tumorigenesis at long-range
claims.chapter: Chernet BT 2014, Transmembrane voltage potential of somatic cells controls oncogene-mediated tumorigenesis at long-range › Abstract
claims.quote: Extending prior work focused on the bioelectric state of cancer cells themselves, we show for the first time that the resting potentials of distant cells are critical for oncogene-dependent tumorigenesis.

claims.title: Oncogene-induced tumor-like structures in Xenopus share hallmarks of human tumors
claims.statement: Tumor-like structures induced in Xenopus laevis tadpoles by human oncogenes such as mutant KRAS display overproliferation, increased nuclear size, hypoxia, intracellular acidity and leukocyte attraction, hallmarks shared with classic human tumors.
claims.author: Michael Levin
claims.work: Transmembrane voltage potential of somatic cells controls oncogene-mediated tumorigenesis at long-range
claims.chapter: Chernet BT 2014, Transmembrane voltage potential of somatic cells controls oncogene-mediated tumorigenesis at long-range › Abstract
claims.quote: In the Xenopus laevis tadpole model, we used human oncogenes such as mutant KRAS to drive formation of tumor-like structures that exhibited overproliferation, increased nuclear size, hypoxia, acidity, and leukocyte attraction.

claims.title: Remote Kv1.5 hyperpolarization suppresses tumor-like structures from two oncogenes
claims.statement: In Xenopus laevis embryos, misexpressing the hyperpolarizing potassium channel Kv1.5 in a blastomere distant from the oncogene-injected blastomere reduces the incidence of induced tumor-like structures by about 35% for Xrel3 and about 29% for Gli1, indicating the suppression is not specific to one oncogene.
claims.author: Michael Levin
claims.work: Transmembrane voltage potential of somatic cells controls oncogene-mediated tumorigenesis at long-range
claims.chapter: Chernet BT 2014, Transmembrane voltage potential of somatic cells controls oncogene-mediated tumorigenesis at long-range › RESULTS › Long-range hyperpolarization suppresses the formation of ITLS
claims.quote: Kv1.5-induced long-distance hyperpolarization was also able to significantly suppress Xrel3 and Gli1 ITLS formation by 34.9% (N=225; t-test, P<0.05) and 29.4% (N=292; t-test, P<0.05), respectively (Fig. 2C), suggesting the effect is not specific for just one type of oncogene.

claims.title: High-chloride hyperpolarization suppresses KRAS tumors, so the effect is ion-independent
claims.statement: Raising extracellular chloride, which hyperpolarizes cells through native chloride channels, decreases the incidence of KRASG12D-induced tumor-like structures in Xenopus laevis embryos by about 38%, showing that tumor suppression depends on the change in membrane voltage rather than on the Kv1.5 channel or on potassium specifically.
claims.author: Michael Levin
claims.work: Transmembrane voltage potential of somatic cells controls oncogene-mediated tumorigenesis at long-range
claims.chapter: Chernet BT 2014, Transmembrane voltage potential of somatic cells controls oncogene-mediated tumorigenesis at long-range › RESULTS › Long-range hyperpolarization suppresses the formation of ITLS
claims.quote: Treatment with high chloride (whose uptake by native Cl− channels hyperpolarizes cells) resulted in a 37.5% decrease (N=349; t-test P<0.05) in KRASG12D ITLS, demonstrating that the suppressive effect is not specific for Kv1.5 nor for potassium, as mediators of the crucial Vmem change (Fig. 2C).

claims.title: Native CLIC1 mediates chloride-based long-range tumor suppression
claims.statement: The endogenous chloride intracellular channel 1 (CLIC1) is required for chloride-driven, long-range suppression of oncogene-induced tumor-like structures in Xenopus laevis, because non-local overexpression of wildtype CLIC1 increases suppression while a dominant-negative CLIC1C24S mutant blocks suppression even under high extracellular chloride.
claims.author: Michael Levin
claims.work: Transmembrane voltage potential of somatic cells controls oncogene-mediated tumorigenesis at long-range
claims.chapter: Chernet BT 2014, Transmembrane voltage potential of somatic cells controls oncogene-mediated tumorigenesis at long-range › RESULTS › Chloride-dependent hyperpolarization through endogenous chloride intracellular channel 1 (CLIC1)
claims.quote: In contrast, overexpression of the mutant CLIC1 (N=336) effectively blocked ITLS suppression despite the presence of high Cl− (Fig 4C). Together, these data suggest a role for native CLIC1 in mediating hyperpolarization-induced long-range ITLS suppression.

claims.title: HDAC1 activity transduces remote voltage change into tumor suppression
claims.statement: Histone deacetylase 1 activity is the main transduction step by which hyperpolarization of distant cells suppresses tumorigenesis in Xenopus laevis, since expressing a dominant-negative HDAC1 at a site remote from KRASG12D-expressing cells raises the incidence of induced tumor-like structures by about 36%.
claims.author: Michael Levin
claims.work: Transmembrane voltage potential of somatic cells controls oncogene-mediated tumorigenesis at long-range
claims.chapter: Chernet BT 2014, Transmembrane voltage potential of somatic cells controls oncogene-mediated tumorigenesis at long-range › RESULTS › Changes in Vmem
claims.quote: introducing DN-HDAC1 non-locally to the site of KRASG12D increased ITLS formation incidence by 35.6% (χ2, P<0.05) (Fig. 5C), suggesting a role for histone deacetylase 1 activity controlling cell behavior at a distance.

claims.title: Antibiotics against gram-positive bacteria increase tumor incidence
claims.statement: Treating Xenopus laevis embryos with antibiotics that target gram-positive bacteria — novobiocin alone, or a cocktail of gentamicin, metronidazole, vancomycin and clindamycin — significantly increases the incidence of oncogene-induced tumor-like structures, implying that native butyrate-producing bacteria normally restrain tumorigenesis.
claims.author: Michael Levin
claims.work: Transmembrane voltage potential of somatic cells controls oncogene-mediated tumorigenesis at long-range
claims.chapter: Chernet BT 2014, Transmembrane voltage potential of somatic cells controls oncogene-mediated tumorigenesis at long-range › RESULTS › Changes in Vmem
claims.quote: Finally, a cocktail of antibiotics (gentamicin, metrodinazole, vancomycin hydrochloride, and clindamycin hydrochloride, all at 20 μM concentration) targeting gram-positive bacteria resulted in a significant increase in ITLS incidence by 26.2% (χ2, P<0.05) (Fig. 6).

claims.title: Vmem controls tumorigenesis via bacterially derived butyrate acting on HDAC1
claims.statement: Control of oncogene-mediated tumorigenesis by resting membrane potential in Xenopus laevis is mediated by histone deacetylase 1, whose inhibition depends on butyrate produced by native gram-positive bacteria.
claims.author: Michael Levin
claims.work: Transmembrane voltage potential of somatic cells controls oncogene-mediated tumorigenesis at long-range
claims.chapter: Chernet BT 2014, Transmembrane voltage potential of somatic cells controls oncogene-mediated tumorigenesis at long-range › RESULTS › Changes in Vmem
claims.quote: Together, these data suggest that the control of tumorigenesis by Vmem is mediated by HDAC1, via butyrate derived from gram-positive bacteria.

claims.title: Tumors may themselves emit bioelectric information detectable at a distance
claims.statement: The authors speculate that long-range bioelectric connections in tumorigenesis are bidirectional, so that in addition to remote tissue voltage influencing tumor growth, tumors may emit bioelectric information that could be detected at a distance.
claims.author: Michael Levin
claims.work: Transmembrane voltage potential of somatic cells controls oncogene-mediated tumorigenesis at long-range
claims.chapter: Chernet BT 2014, Transmembrane voltage potential of somatic cells controls oncogene-mediated tumorigenesis at long-range › DISCUSSION › Long-range control of tumorigenic process by Vmem
claims.quote: It is tempting to speculate that the long-range connections are bi-directional: not only does remote electrical state of tissue matter for tumor growth, but perhaps tumors also emit bioelectrical information that could be detectable at a distance.

claims.title: Resting potential as a systems-level causal factor rather than specific channels
claims.statement: Because tumor suppression was obtained with either chloride- or potassium-based hyperpolarization, the authors argue that a systems-level physiological property — resting membrane potential — rather than any specific ion channel acting as an oncogene or tumor suppressor, can be a powerful causal factor regulating tumorigenesis.
claims.author: Michael Levin
claims.work: Transmembrane voltage potential of somatic cells controls oncogene-mediated tumorigenesis at long-range
claims.chapter: Chernet BT 2014, Transmembrane voltage potential of somatic cells controls oncogene-mediated tumorigenesis at long-range › DISCUSSION › Long-range control of tumorigenic process by Vmem
claims.quote: Thus, in complement to the gene-focused idea of specific ion channels being intrinsic oncogenes or tumor suppressors [44, 48, 145], we suggest that a systems-level physiological property – resting potential – can be a powerful causal factor in regulating these processes.

claims.title: Hyperpolarization skews butyrate-producing bacteria toward depolarized oncogene cells
claims.statement: In the model the authors propose, hyperpolarized cells present a positively charged outer surface that reduces bacterial viability, so butyrate-producing bacteria are distributed away from hyperpolarized cells and toward the depolarized oncogene-expressing cells, where the resulting butyrate inhibits HDAC and promotes histone hyperacetylation and cell cycle arrest.

claims.work: Transmembrane voltage potential of somatic cells controls oncogene-mediated tumorigenesis at long-range

claims.quote: As a result, distribution of butyrate producing-bacteria is skewed away from hyperpolarized cells in favor of oncogene-expressing cells, which are known to be depolarized pre-neoplastic transformation [43].

claims.title: If conserved in mammals, Vmem modulation offers cancer detection and treatment routes
claims.statement: The authors predict that if the role of remote endogenous bioelectric states in tumorigenesis is conserved in mammalian cancer models, modulation of resting membrane potential — potentially with ion channel drugs already approved for human use — would provide new cancer detection and treatment modalities.

claims.work: Transmembrane voltage potential of somatic cells controls oncogene-mediated tumorigenesis at long-range

claims.quote: Future work must also examine the roles of remote endogenous bioelectric states in mammalian cancer models; if conserved, these data suggest a number of detection and treatment modalities focused on Vmem modulation.

claims.title: Embryonic nicotine exposure causes major brain malformations in Xenopus
claims.statement: Exposing Xenopus laevis embryos to nicotine (0.1 mg/mL, stages 10–35) causes major brain morphology defects (absent nostrils, forebrain or midbrain, misformed hindbrain) in about 55% of tadpoles at stage 45, compared with about 6% of controls.

claims.work: HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns

claims.quote: Nicotine exposure caused a significantly high incidence of major brain morphology defects (~55%) in comparison to controls (~6%).

claims.title: BETSE model: leak and Kir channels produce a hyperpolarized neural tube prepattern
claims.statement: In a BETSE bioelectric model of the stage 15 Xenopus neurula, regional differences in K+ and Cl− leak permeability open Kir channels in the neural tube, producing a Vmem of about −50 mV there while the neural folds and ectoderm stay near −5 mV, matching observed embryonic Vmem patterns.
claims.author: Michael Levin
claims.work: HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns
claims.chapter: Pai VP 2018, HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns › Results › Model of Vmem
claims.quote: This results in open Kir channels in the hyperpolarized neural tube region leading to a Vmem pattern of approximately −50 mV in the neural tube region, while the lateral neural folds and ectoderm remain at ~−5 mV (Fig. 3a, e).

claims.title: Nicotine depolarizes the neural plate prepattern by about 15 mV, as the model predicted
claims.statement: In stage 15 Xenopus embryos, nicotine treatment significantly reduces the endogenous neural hyperpolarization signal (a depolarization of about 15 mV, measured by calibrated voltage-dye imaging), matching the BETSE model's prediction in direction and magnitude.
claims.author: Michael Levin
claims.work: HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns
claims.chapter: Pai VP 2018, HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns › Results › Nicotine targets Vmem
claims.quote: Nicotine-treated embryos showed significant reduction in endogenous neural Vmem signal (depolarization by ~15 mV) in comparison to controls (Figs. 4a, b, e, f, and Supplementary Figure 1). This observation matches the BETSE model predictions of nicotine effect on Vmem both in direction (depolarization) and magnitude (~15 mV).

claims.title: Nicotine causes brain defects by disrupting the endogenous bioelectric prepattern
claims.statement: The authors' BETSE model explains nicotine-induced brain defects in Xenopus as resulting from nicotine's disruption of the endogenous bioelectric prepattern (neural tube hyperpolarization) required for brain development.
claims.author: Michael Levin
claims.work: HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns
claims.chapter: Pai VP 2018, HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns › Results › Nicotine targets Vmem
claims.quote: Our model explains why nicotine induces brain defects: it correctly predicts the disruptive effects of this teratogen on the endogenous bioelectric prepattern required for brain development.

claims.title: Normal brain patterning needs the Vmem difference between neural tube and lateral tissue
claims.statement: In Xenopus brain development, it is the spatial contrast of Vmem that matters: depolarizing the neural tube region or hyperpolarizing the lateral regions both cause brain defects, because the precise differential bioelectric state induces the balance of proliferation, apoptosis and gene expression needed to build a normal brain.
claims.author: Michael Levin
claims.work: HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns
claims.chapter: Pai VP 2018, HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns › Results › BETSE model identifies HCN2 channel as a repair reagent
claims.quote: The spatial patterning is crucial, as both depolarization of the middle region, or hyperpolarization of the lateral regions, both cause brain defects—it is the precise differential bioelectric state that induces the required balance of proliferation, apoptosis, and gene expression to build a normal brain28,48.

claims.title: HCN2 modelled as a voltage-controlled switch that amplifies small Vmem gradients
claims.statement: In the BETSE model of the Xenopus neurula, HCN2 channels open at hyperpolarized membrane voltage and hyperpolarize further when open, so they act as a voltage-controlled switch that amplifies small existing Vmem gradients: sufficiently negative neural tube cells go very hyperpolarized while depolarized lateral regions are left unchanged.
claims.author: Michael Levin
claims.work: HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns
claims.chapter: Pai VP 2018, HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns › Results › BETSE model identifies HCN2 channel as a repair reagent
claims.quote: HCN2 channels are predicted to open at hyperpolarized Vmem, generating more hyperpolarization with opening, thereby serving as a Vmem-controlled switch of Vmem state, capable of amplifying small Vmem gradients, similar to IT effect (Fig. 3c, e, f).

claims.title: BETSE model predicts HCN2 maintains the neural tube Vmem pattern despite nicotine
claims.statement: The BETSE model predicts that uniformly expressed HCN2 channels, which open at hyperpolarized Vmem and so amplify small Vmem gradients, open preferentially in the Xenopus neural tube and maintain its hyperpolarized Vmem pattern even in nicotine-exposed model embryos.
claims.author: Michael Levin
claims.work: HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns
claims.chapter: Pai VP 2018, HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns › Results › BETSE model identifies HCN2 channel as a repair reagent
claims.quote: Importantly, our model predicts that HCN2 expression leads to maintenance of neural tube Vmem pattern even in nicotine-exposed model embryos, similar to the action of IT (Fig. 3c vs. d, e, f).

claims.title: Measured HCN2 hyperpolarization in vivo was about half the model's prediction
claims.statement: Hcn2 mRNA injection hyperpolarized the neural Vmem signal of Xenopus embryos by about 15 mV relative to controls, whereas the BETSE model predicted about 30 mV.
claims.author: Michael Levin
claims.work: HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns
claims.chapter: Pai VP 2018, HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns › Results › HCN2 corrects Vmem
claims.quote: However, the extent of enhanced hyperpolarization predicted by BETSE model for IT and HCN2 was higher (~30 mV) than actually observed (~15 mV) (Figs. 3e and 4).

claims.title: HCN2 expression restores the neural Vmem prepattern despite nicotine
claims.statement: In nicotine-exposed Xenopus embryos, expression of HCN2 channels enhances the neural-tube-specific hyperpolarization and restores the endogenous Vmem prepattern that nicotine otherwise suppresses, as the BETSE model predicted.
claims.author: Michael Levin
claims.work: HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns
claims.chapter: Pai VP 2018, HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns › Results › HCN2 corrects Vmem
claims.quote: As predicted, nicotine exposure suppresses the neural brain-specific Vmem pattern, while HCN2 channel expression enhances the neural Vmem pattern and restores it even in presence of the otherwise teratogenic nicotine.

claims.title: HCN2 reduces even minor background brain defects in untreated embryos
claims.statement: In untreated Xenopus embryos, Hcn2 mRNA injection reduced the incidence of minor deviations from ideal brain morphology from about 9% to about 1.5%, so HCN2 improved patterning beyond that of unperturbed controls.
claims.author: Michael Levin
claims.work: HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns
claims.chapter: Pai VP 2018, HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns › Results › HCN2 overexpression reduces background brain defects
claims.quote: Thus, misexpression of HCN2 channels resulted in an improvement of developmental patterning even beyond that observed in control populations of unperturbed embryos raised under optimal conditions.

claims.title: HCN2 fully rescues nicotine-induced brain malformations to control levels
claims.statement: Injection of Hcn2-WT mRNA into nicotine-exposed Xenopus embryos reduced the incidence of major brain morphology defects from about 60% to about 6%, indistinguishable from untreated controls (about 7%).
claims.author: Michael Levin
claims.work: HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns
claims.chapter: Pai VP 2018, HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns › Results › HCN2 rescues nicotine exposure-induced brain defects
claims.quote: Remarkably, Hcn2-WT mRNA-injected embryos showed a complete rescue of brain morphology defects from nicotine exposure, to levels (~6%) indistinguishable from that of untreated control embryos (~7%) (Fig. 5f).

claims.title: Dominant-negative HCN2 does not rescue nicotine brain defects
claims.statement: Nicotine-exposed Xenopus embryos injected with a dominant-negative, non-conducting HCN2 mutant showed no rescue of brain morphology defects (about 70% defective), so the rescue depends on HCN2 channel conductance.
claims.author: Michael Levin
claims.work: HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns
claims.chapter: Pai VP 2018, HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns › Results › HCN2 rescues nicotine exposure-induced brain defects
claims.quote: In contrast, nicotine-exposed embryos injected with a mutant, dominant-negative form of HCN2 failed to show rescue of brain morphology defects (~70%) (Fig. 5f).

claims.title: HCN2 restores wild-type brain shape in nicotine-exposed tadpoles
claims.statement: Geometric morphometrics of stage-45 tadpoles show that nicotine significantly changes brain shape relative to the head, while nicotine-exposed tadpoles injected with Hcn2-WT mRNA do not differ in shape from controls.
claims.author: Michael Levin
claims.work: HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns
claims.chapter: Pai VP 2018, HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns › Results › HCN2 rescues nicotine exposure-induced brain defects
claims.quote: Thus, nicotine significantly changes brain shape, but Hcn2-WT mRNA microinjections restore brain morphology to the wild-type state.

claims.title: HCN2 restores learning in nicotine-exposed tadpoles
claims.statement: In an automated red-light avoidance assay, only about 12% of nicotine-exposed Xenopus tadpoles learned, versus 100% of controls, and about 85% of nicotine-exposed tadpoles injected with Hcn2-WT mRNA learned.
claims.author: Michael Levin
claims.work: HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns
claims.chapter: Pai VP 2018, HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns › Results › HCN2 restores learning in nicotine-exposed larvae
claims.quote: However, nicotine-exposed embryos receiving Hcn2-WT mRNA showed significant improvement in learning ability (85%, n = 20) in comparison to nicotine-exposed tadpoles (Fig. 7b, c, ANOVA, p < 0.001).

claims.title: HCN2 rescue corrects otx2 and xbf1 expression after nicotine
claims.statement: Nicotine reduces or mispatterns expression of the forebrain/midbrain transcription factors otx2 and xbf1 in Xenopus embryos, and Hcn2-WT mRNA injection restores their normal expression, linking HCN2-mediated repair to the known genetic cascade of brain patterning.
claims.author: Michael Levin
claims.work: HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns
claims.chapter: Pai VP 2018, HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns › Results › HCN2 restores marker expression in nicotine-treated embryos
claims.quote: Thus, HCN2 channel rescue of nicotine-induced defects includes correction of otx2 and xbf1, connecting HCN2-mediated repair of brain to the known molecular-genetic cascade of brain patterning factors.

claims.title: Native HCN2 activity is not required for normal brain patterning
claims.statement: Because a dominant-negative HCN2 construct does not disrupt brain patterning, native HCN2 channel activity is not required for normal Xenopus brain patterning, ruling out the possibility that nicotine causes defects by directly blocking endogenous HCN2.
claims.author: Michael Levin
claims.work: HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns
claims.chapter: Pai VP 2018, HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns › Discussion
claims.quote: However, our experiments with dominant-negative HCN2 channel shows that native HCN2 channel activity is not required for proper brain patterning (Supplementary Figure 4), thus negating this possibility.

claims.title: HCN2's restorative action may extend to many teratogens and lesions
claims.statement: The authors suggest that HCN2's ability to improve brain morphology even in control embryos points to a general mechanism, reinforcing endogenous bioelectric signals needed for correct brain morphology, that could repair defects caused by a wide range of teratogens or physiological and genetic lesions, not only nicotine.
claims.author: Michael Levin
claims.work: HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns
claims.chapter: Pai VP 2018, HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns › Discussion
claims.quote: These observations suggest that the restorative action of HCN2 is not limited to nicotine-induced brain morphology defects, but could reveal a more general mechanism of action, reinforcing the endogenous bioelectrical signals required for correct developmental brain morphology that might be partially destabilized by a wide range of exogenous teratogens or endogenous physiological/genetic lesions.

claims.title: Reagents that sharpen bioelectric compartment borders reinforce normal patterning
claims.statement: The BETSE model predicts that reagents that sharpen the borders between bioelectric compartments, such as the context-sensitive HCN2 channel, will reinforce normal developmental patterning, a prediction confirmed for HCN2 in vivo.
