claims.quote: this applies (among animals breathing air and having a lung) to all birds and oviparous quadrupeds. For all these have their testes internal near the loin

claims.title: The uterus is always double
claims.statement: The uterus is always double, just as the testes of the male are always two.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book I, Part 3
claims.quote: The uterus is always double, just as the testes are always two in the male.

claims.title: Animals with only ducts or internal testes copulate more quickly
claims.statement: Animals that have no testes but only ducts, or that have internal testes, are all quicker in accomplishing copulation than animals with external testes.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book I, Part 4
claims.quote: so those which have not testes but only ducts, or which have them indeed but internally, are all quicker in accomplishing copulation.

claims.title: Seasonally breeding birds' testes swell in the breeding season and shrink after
claims.statement: Birds' testes are much enlarged at the time of copulation, and in birds that pair at one season of the year they become so small afterwards as to be almost indiscernible.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book I, Part 4
claims.quote: for their testes are much enlarged at the time of copulation, and all those which pair at one season of the year have them so small when this is past that they are almost indiscernible

claims.title: Hedgehogs copulate standing upright because of their spines
claims.statement: Hedgehogs do not mount the female from behind like other quadrupeds but copulate standing upright, because of their spines.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book I, Part 5
claims.quote: for the hedgehog does not, like the other quadrupeds, mount upon the back of the female, but they conjugate standing upright because of their spines.

claims.title: Cartilaginous fishes and vipers bear live young from eggs formed inside
claims.statement: Cartilaginous fishes and vipers first produce eggs internally and then bring forth their young alive.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book I, Part 10
claims.quote: But the cartilaginous fish and the vipers produce their young alive externally, but first produce eggs internally.

claims.title: Ovoviviparous animals keep their eggs inside because they are cold
claims.statement: Cartilaginous fishes and vipers do not lay their eggs outside because they are of a cold nature, which leaves the egg-shell soft and unprotected.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book I, Part 10
claims.quote: It is because they are of a cold nature, not hot as some assert, that they do not lay their eggs externally.

claims.title: Elephant and hedgehog have internal testes because their skin is unsuitable
claims.statement: The testes are internal in the elephant and the hedgehog, because their skin is not suited to form a separate protective covering (scrotum) for them.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book I, Part 12
claims.quote: For the same reason they are internal in the elephant and hedgehog, for the skin of these, too, is not well suited to keep the protective part separate.

claims.title: Cephalopods copulate mouth to mouth with arms entwined
claims.statement: Cephalopods copulate by entwining at the mouth, pushing against one another and enfolding their arms.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book I, Part 15
claims.quote: The cephalopoda entwine together at the mouth, pushing against one another and enfolding their arms.

claims.title: The octopus arm inserted in the female's funnel is not a generative organ
claims.statement: The arm that the male octopus inserts into the female's funnel serves only for attachment and is not an organ useful for generation, being outside the male's seminal passage.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book I, Part 15
claims.quote: is only for the sake of attachment, and it is not an organ useful for generation, for it is outside the passage in the male and indeed outside the body of the male altogether.

claims.title: Fleas, flies and cantharides arise from putrefying matter
claims.statement: Some insects, such as fleas, flies and cantharides, do not come from parents but from putrefying matter, and although they unite and generate, they produce only a scolex (larva), not a creature of their own kind.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book I, Part 16
claims.quote: these insects do not come into being from animals but from putrefying matter, liquid or solid; such are fleas, flies, and cantharides.

claims.title: In most mating insects the female is larger than the male
claims.statement: In most insects that copulate, the female is larger than the male.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book I, Part 16
claims.quote: In most of those which unite the female is larger than the male.

claims.title: In most insects the female inserts a part into the male
claims.statement: In most insects the male does not insert any part into the female; instead the female inserts a part of herself from below upwards into the male.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book I, Part 16
claims.quote: In most cases the male does not insert any part into the female, but the female from below upwards into the male

claims.title: Resemblances to ancestors can skip generations
claims.statement: Children may resemble remote ancestors from whom nothing has come to them, since resemblances recur after an interval of generations.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book I, Part 18
claims.quote: Further, children are like their more remote ancestors from whom nothing has come, for the resemblances recur at an interval of many generations

claims.title: Mutilated parents do not always have mutilated young
claims.statement: The young of mutilated parents are not always mutilated, just as young are not always like their parents.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book I, Part 18
claims.quote: And the young of mutilated parents are not always mutilated, just as they are not always like their parents

claims.title: Semen does not come from all parts of the body
claims.statement: Semen is not drawn from every part of the parent's body, contrary to those who explain inheritance that way.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book I, Part 18
claims.quote: Into this we must next inquire, since it is plain that the semen is not secreted from all the parts.

claims.title: Large animals have few young, small animals many
claims.statement: Large animals have few young and small animals have many.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book I, Part 18
claims.quote: A further proof that it is not a waste-product, but rather a secretion, is the fact that the large animals have few young, the small many.

claims.title: Humans gain half their adult height in about the first five years
claims.statement: In human beings the body gains in about the first five years half the height that it gains in all the rest of life.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book I, Part 18
claims.quote: for in about five years, in the case of human beings at any rate, the body seems to gain half the height that is gained in all the rest of life.

claims.title: Fat people are less fertile because the secretion turns to fat
claims.statement: Fat people, women as well as men, are less fertile than others, because in the well-nourished the secretion being concocted turns to fat instead of semen.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book I, Part 18
claims.quote: And fat people, women as well as men, appear to be less fertile than others from the fact that the secretion when in process of concoction turns to fat with those who are too well-nourished.

claims.title: Semen is a secretion of useful nutriment in its last stage
claims.statement: Semen is a secretion (residue) of useful nutriment in its final stage, not a waste-product of the body.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book I, Part 18
claims.quote: From what has been said, it is clear that semen is a secretion of useful nutriment, and that in its last stage, whether it is produced by all or no.

claims.title: Semen and menstruation begin at the same age
claims.statement: Semen begins to appear in males at the same time of life as the menstrual flow begins in females, together with the change of voice and the development of the breasts.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book I, Part 19
claims.quote: For the semen begins to appear in males and to be emitted at the same time of life that the catamenia begin to flow in females

claims.title: Among viviparous animals females are smaller because of menstruation
claims.statement: Among the viviparous animals females are smaller than males, because the secretion that would build the body is discharged as menstrual fluid, and this is the only class that menstruates.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book I, Part 19
claims.quote: the same cause accounts for the fact that the bulk of the body is smaller in females than in males among the vivipara, since this is the only class in which the catamenia are discharged from the body.

claims.title: The female is a kind of impotent male, unable to concoct semen
claims.statement: The female is, as it were, an impotent male: she is female through an incapacity to concoct the final nutriment into semen.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book I, Part 20
claims.quote: the woman is as it were an impotent male, for it is through a certain incapacity that the female is female, being incapable of concocting the nutriment in its last stage into semen

claims.title: All directly viviparous animals menstruate, though less than women
claims.statement: All animals that are viviparous without first producing eggs (man and the viviparous quadrupeds) have a menstrual discharge, unless defective like the mule, though the discharge is not as abundant as in women.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book I, Part 20
claims.quote: all these have the catamenia, unless they are defective in development as the mule, only the efflux is not abundant as in women.

claims.title: Menstruation usually begins when the breasts have risen two fingers' breadth
claims.statement: Menstruation generally begins in girls when the breasts have risen two fingers' breadth.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book I, Part 20
claims.quote: for it is when they have risen two fingers’ breadth that the catamenia generally begin.

claims.title: Nothing material from the male need enter the embryo; he imparts motion and form
claims.statement: Nothing material from the male needs to become part of the embryo; what comes from him acts only by imparting motion and form, as the medical art cures a patient.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book I, Part 21
claims.quote: It is plain then that it is not necessary that anything at all should come away from the male, and if anything does come away it does not follow that this gives rise to the embryo as being in the embryo, but only as that which imparts the motion and as the form

claims.title: A hen producing wind-eggs can be made fertile by treading while the egg is yellow
claims.statement: If a hen producing wind-eggs is trodden by a cock before the egg has begun to whiten, while it is still all yolk, the eggs become fertile instead of wind-eggs.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book I, Part 21
claims.quote: For if a hen-bird is in process of producing wind-eggs and is then trodden by the cock before the egg has begun to whiten and while it is all still yellow, then they become fertile instead of being wind-eggs.

claims.title: A hen trodden by a second cock while the egg is yellow bears chicks like the second
claims.statement: If a hen is trodden by a second cock while her eggs are still yolk, the whole brood of chicks turns out like the second cock.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book I, Part 21
claims.quote: And if while it is still yellow she be trodden by another cock, the whole brood of chicks turn out like the second cock.

claims.title: In oviparous fishes only the eggs reached by the milt are fertilized
claims.statement: In oviparous fishes the male sprinkles milt over the eggs after they are laid, and only the eggs the milt reaches are fertilized.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book I, Part 21
claims.quote: When the female has laid her eggs, the male spinkles the milt over them, and those eggs are fertilized which it reaches, but not the others

claims.title: In all animals that move about the sexes are separate
claims.statement: In all animals that can move about, the sexes are separate, one individual male and another female of the same species, whereas in plants they are combined.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book I, Part 23
claims.quote: In all animals which can move about, the sexes are separated, one individual being male and one female, though both are the same in species, as with man and horse.

claims.title: Generation makes kinds eternal as species, not as individuals
claims.statement: Animals generate because a living thing cannot be eternal as an individual but can be eternal as a species, which is why there is always a race of men, animals and plants.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book II
claims.quote: Now it is impossible for it to be eternal as an individual (though of course the real essence of things is in the individual)— were it such it would be eternal — but it is possible for it as a species.

claims.title: Animals with blood are larger than bloodless ones, and mobile larger than fixed
claims.statement: Taken generally, animals with blood are larger than bloodless animals, and animals that move about are larger than those that stay fixed.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book II
claims.quote: Therefore, taking a general view, we may say that sanguinea are of greater size than bloodless animals, and those which move about than those which remain fixed.

claims.title: Eggs of fishes, crustaceans and cephalopods grow after being laid
claims.statement: The eggs of birds and oviparous reptiles are complete when laid and do not grow, whereas the eggs of fishes, crustaceans and cephalopods are imperfect and increase in size after being laid.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book II
claims.quote: The eggs of others are imperfect; such are those of fishes, crustaceans, and cephalopods, for their eggs increase after being produced.

claims.title: All viviparous animals have blood
claims.statement: All viviparous animals have blood, and animals with blood are either viviparous or oviparous unless altogether infertile.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book II
claims.quote: All the vivipara are sanguineous, and the sanguinea are either viviparous or oviparous, except those which are altogether infertile.

claims.title: Only air-breathing animals are internally viviparous
claims.statement: No animal is internally viviparous unless it takes in and breathes out air.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book II
claims.quote: for nothing is internally viviparous unless it receive and breathe out air.

claims.title: Animals with lungs are hotter than animals without
claims.statement: Animals with a lung are generally hotter than those without, and among them those whose lung is soft and full of blood are hottest.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book II
claims.quote: for generally those animals which have a lung are hotter than those which have not

claims.title: Heat and dryness explain why birds and reptiles lay complete eggs
claims.statement: Birds and scaly reptiles lay a complete egg because they are hot, but only an egg rather than live young because they are dry; the reproductive mode follows from an animal's heat and moisture.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book II
claims.quote: For birds and scaly reptiles because of their heat produce a perfect egg, but because of their dryness it is only an egg

claims.title: All insects produce a scolex and all insects are bloodless
claims.statement: All insects produce a scolex (larva), all insects are bloodless, and so every animal that produces a scolex is bloodless.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book II
claims.quote: All insects produce a scolex. Now all the insects are bloodless, wherefore all creatures that produce a scolex from themselves are so.

claims.title: Nature orders generation in a graded series by heat and perfection
claims.statement: Nature orders generation in a regular gradation: the hottest and most perfect animals bear live young internally, then come those viviparous after internal eggs, then those laying perfect eggs, then those laying imperfect eggs, and coldest of all those producing a scolex.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book II
claims.quote: We must observe how rightly Nature orders generation in regular gradation. The more perfect and hotter animals produce their young perfect in respect of quality

claims.title: Embryonic parts form in succession, not all together
claims.statement: The parts of an embryo do not all exist from the start; some are visible in the embryo while others are not yet formed, so they come into being in succession.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book II
claims.quote: That the former is not the fact is plain even to the senses, for some of the parts are clearly visible as already existing in the embryo while others are not

claims.title: The lung appears later than the heart in development though larger
claims.statement: In development the lung appears later than the heart, even though it is larger, so late appearance is not due to small size.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book II
claims.quote: for the lung is of greater size than the heart, and yet appears later than the heart in the original development.

claims.title: Semen is thick and white when emitted and becomes watery on cooling
claims.statement: Semen is thick and white when it issues from the body but on cooling becomes liquid and colourless like water, and in frost it liquefies rather than freezing.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book II
claims.quote: For whereas when it issues from the animal it is thick and white, yet on cooling it becomes liquid as water, and its colour is that of water.

claims.title: Semen is always white, including that of Ethiopians
claims.statement: Semen is invariably white, so Herodotus was wrong that the semen of Ethiopians is black.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book II
claims.quote: for it is also an invariable rule that it is white, and Herodotus does not report the truth when he says that the semen of the Aethiopians is black

claims.title: General animal characters develop before those of the species
claims.statement: An embryo does not become an animal and a particular kind of animal at the same time; the characters peculiar to the species develop last.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book II
claims.quote: For e.g. an animal does not become at the same time an animal and a man or a horse or any other particular animal. For the end is developed last, and the peculiar character of the species is the end of the generation in each individual.

claims.title: Reason alone enters from outside and is divine
claims.statement: Of the kinds of soul, reason alone enters the embryo from outside and alone is divine, since its activity has no connection with any bodily activity.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book II
claims.quote: It remains, then, for the reason alone so to enter and alone to be divine, for no bodily activity has any connexion with the activity of reason.

claims.title: Some cartilaginous fishes complete development by connection to the uterus
claims.statement: In some cartilaginous fishes, once the nutriment of the egg is used up, the embryo completes its development by connection with the uterus, so the egg is not released from the uterus.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book II
claims.quote: in other cases, when the nutriment from the egg is consumed, development is completed by connection with the uterus, and therefore the egg is not set free from the uterus.

claims.title: Menstruation tends to come during the waning of the moon
claims.statement: The menstrual period in women is not exactly fixed but tends to come during the waning of the moon, because bodies are colder when the environment is colder.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book II
claims.quote: The period is not accurately defined in women, but tends to return during the waning of the moon.

claims.title: Hybrids come to resemble the female line over successive generations
claims.statement: When different kinds are crossed, the first cross resembles both parents, but over successive generations the offspring come to resemble the female in form.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book II
claims.quote: the first cross has a common resemblance to both parents, as the hybrid between fox and dog, partridge and domestic fowl, but as time goes on and one generation springs from another, the final result resembles the female in form

claims.title: The heart is the first part to be distinctly formed in all animals with blood
claims.statement: In all animals with blood the heart is the first part to appear distinctly formed in the embryo, being the origin of the blood-vessels and of the other parts.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book II
claims.quote: Therefore it is that the heart appears first distinctly marked off in all the sanguinea

claims.title: No male of the erythrinus has ever been seen
claims.statement: No male of the fish called erythrinus has ever been seen, only females and specimens full of roe, which suggests it may generate without a male.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book II
claims.quote: No male of the so-called erythrinus has ever yet been seen, but females, and specimens full of roe, have been seen.

claims.title: Eels and some mullets are neither male nor female
claims.statement: Some fishes are neither male nor female, such as eels and a kind of mullet found in stagnant waters.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book II
claims.quote: Again, some members of the class of fishes are neither male nor female, as eels and a kind of mullets found in stagnant waters.

claims.title: Nature makes nothing in vain, so the male is needed for full generation
claims.statement: Where the sexes are separate the female cannot generate perfectly alone, for otherwise the male would exist in vain, and Nature makes nothing in vain.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book II
claims.quote: But whenever the sexes are separate the female cannot generate perfectly by herself alone, for then the male would exist in vain, and Nature makes nothing in vain.

claims.title: Internal parts form before external parts in the embryo
claims.statement: In the embryo the internal parts come into being before the external, and the larger become visible before the smaller.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book II
claims.quote: After this, as said already, the internal parts come into being before the external.

claims.title: Polydactylous quadrupeds bear blind young whose eyelids open after birth
claims.statement: All polydactylous (many-toed) quadrupeds, such as the dog, lion, wolf, fox and jackal, bear their young blind, and the eyelids do not separate until after birth.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book II
claims.quote: Moreover, all polydactylous quadrupeds, as dog, lion, wolf, fox, jackal, produce their young blind, and the eyelids do not separate till after birth.

claims.title: In the early embryo the head and eyes are largest and the legs small
claims.statement: In the embryo at an early stage the parts about the head, especially the eyes, appear largest and the parts below the navel, such as the legs, are small, because the lower parts exist for the sake of the upper.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book II
claims.quote: This is why the parts about the head, and particularly the eyes, appear largest in the embryo at an early stage, while the parts below the umbilicus, as the legs, are small

claims.title: Eyes appear very large early but are the last parts to be completed
claims.statement: The eyes of all animals, whether walking, swimming or flying, appear very large from the beginning of development but are the last parts to be completely formed, collapsing in the interval.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book II
claims.quote: Though from the beginning they appear very large in all creatures, whether they walk or swim or fly, yet they are the last of the parts to be formed completely, for in the intervening time they collapse.

claims.title: The bregma is the last bone to form and is still soft after birth
claims.statement: The bregma (the top of the skull) is the last bone to be formed and is still soft in children after birth, more so in man than in other animals because man's brain is the most fluid and largest.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book II
claims.quote: For this reason the ‘bregma’ is the last of the bones to be formed; even after birth this bone is still soft in children.

claims.title: Bones set the limit of an animal's size
claims.statement: Bones grow only up to a certain point, and they set the limit of size in animals; if bones could always grow, every animal with bone or its analogue would grow as long as it lived.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book II
claims.quote: if these had been always able to grow, all animals that have bone or its analogue would grow as long as they lived, for these set the limit of size to animals.

claims.title: Hair goes on growing after death
claims.statement: Hair continues to grow after death, though it does not begin growing then.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book II
claims.quote: Hair actually goes on growing after death; it does not, however, begin growing then.

claims.title: Of all bones only the teeth grow throughout life
claims.statement: Of all the bones, the teeth alone go on growing throughout life, as shown by teeth that grow out of line until they no longer meet.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book II
claims.quote: Of all the bones they alone go on growing through life, as is plain with the teeth which grow out of the straight line so as no longer to touch each other.

claims.title: Other animals are born with teeth but man is born without
claims.statement: Other animals are born with teeth or their analogue, because they are more perfect at birth than man, whereas man is normally born without teeth.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book II
claims.quote: Other animals are born in possession of teeth or their analogue (unless in cases contrary to Nature), because when they are set free from the parent they are more perfect than man; but man (also unless in cases contrary to Nature) is born without them.

claims.title: Man is the most naked animal and has the smallest nails for his size
claims.statement: Man is the most naked of all animals and has the smallest nails in proportion to his size, because he has the least earthy residue.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book II
claims.quote: man is the most naked in body of all animals and has the smallest nails in proportion to his size

claims.title: Umbilical cord vessel number rises with animal size
claims.statement: The umbilical cord consists of blood-vessels in a sheath: more numerous in larger animals such as cattle, one in the smallest animals, and two in those of intermediate size.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book II
claims.quote: The cord consists of blood-vessels in a sheath, more numerous in the larger animals as cattle and the like, one in the smallest, two in those of intermediate size.

claims.title: Animals lacking upper front teeth have cotyledons in the uterus
claims.statement: All animals without front teeth in the upper jaw, and those with front teeth in both jaws whose uterus has many close blood-vessels rather than one great one, have cotyledons in the uterus; most with front teeth in both jaws and no horns lack them.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book II
claims.quote: All animals with no front teeth in the upper jaw, and all those which have them in both jaws and whose uterus has not one great blood-vessel running through it but many close together insteadall these have in the uterus the so-called cotyledons

claims.title: Cotyledons shrink and disappear as the embryo matures
claims.statement: As the embryo grows and approaches completion, the cotyledons in the uterus become smaller and finally disappear when it is fully formed.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book II
claims.quote: As the embryo grows and approaches perfection the cotyledons become smaller and finally disappear when it is perfected.

claims.title: Of all hybrids only mules are sterile
claims.statement: Animals born of crosses between different kinds can all mate and produce young of both sexes, except mules, which alone are sterile.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book II
claims.quote: Of the animals that arise from such union all except mules are found to copulate again with each other and to be able to produce young of both sexes, but mules alone are sterile

claims.title: General theories not based on the special principles of a subject are empty
claims.statement: All theories not based on the special principles of the subject in question are empty: in natural science one must reason from the facts peculiar to the kinds concerned, as geometry reasons from geometrical principles.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book II
claims.quote: For all theories not based on the special principles involved are empty; they only appear to be connected with the facts without being so really.

claims.title: The ass cannot bear cold and is not found in cold regions
claims.statement: The ass is of a cold nature and cannot bear cold, so it is not produced in wintry regions such as Scythia and the land of the Celts beyond Iberia.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book II
claims.quote: Again the ass is an animal of cold nature, and so is not wont to be produced in wintry regions because it cannot bear cold, as in Scythia and the neighbouring country and among the Celts beyond Iberia

claims.title: The gestation period of both horse and ass is one year
claims.statement: The period of gestation in both the horse and the ass is one year, so the mother gives birth in the same season as she was impregnated.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book II
claims.quote: for the mothers bear at the same season as that in which they are impregnated, the period of gestation in both horse and ass being one year.

claims.title: The mule is sterile because the ass's cold seed chills the horse's
claims.statement: Mules are sterile because the horse already tends to sterility and becomes wholly so when its generative secretion is chilled by mixing with the cold secretion of the ass.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book II
claims.quote: The horse is much the same; it tends naturally towards sterility, and to make it entirely so it is only necessary that its generative secretion should become colder; now this is what happens to it when mixed with the corresponding secretion of the ass.

claims.title: A female mule can conceive but cannot carry the foal to birth
claims.statement: A female mule can sometimes conceive, but she cannot nourish the embryo to birth because she has no menstrual secretion.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book II
claims.quote: Hence it is sometimes possible for the female to conceive, as has been known to happen before now, but it is impossible for her to complete the process of nourishing the embryo and bringing it to birth.

claims.title: Selachians are internally oviparous but bring forth live young
claims.statement: The cartilaginous fishes form an egg inside the uterus but give birth to live young; their egg is soft-shelled and of one colour.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book III
claims.quote: The cartilaginous fishes, as has been often said already, are oviparous internally but produce the young alive, the egg changing previously from one part of the uterus to another; and their egg is soft-shelled and of one colour.

claims.title: Wind-eggs occur in heavy, prolific birds, not in birds of prey
claims.statement: Unfertilised 'wind-eggs' are produced by birds that are not strong fliers or predators and that produce many young, not by birds of prey.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book III
claims.quote: Some embryos are formed in birds spontaneously, which are called wind-eggs and ‘zephyria’ by some; these occur in birds which are not given to flight nor rapine but which produce many young

claims.title: Birds of prey lay few eggs because residual matter goes to wings
claims.statement: Because both wings and semen are made from the same residual matter, birds whose residue goes into wings and feathers (birds of prey) mate little and lay few eggs.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book III
claims.quote: Since then both the wings and the semen are made from residual matter, nature cannot afford to spend much upon both. And for this same reason the birds of prey are neither given to treading much nor to laying many eggs

claims.title: The cuckoo lays few eggs and lays them in other birds' nests
claims.statement: The cuckoo, though not a bird of prey, lays few eggs, and it lays them in the nests of other birds; Aristotle attributes this to its cold, cowardly nature.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book III
claims.quote: The cuckoo, though not a bird of prey, lays few eggs, because it is of a cold nature, as is shown by the cowardice of the bird, whereas a generative animal should be hot and moist. That it is cowardly is plain, for it is pursued by all the birds and lays eggs in the nests of others.

claims.title: The lioness bears five or six cubs, then fewer each year, then none
claims.statement: A lioness produces five or six cubs at her first birth, four the next year, then three, and so down to one and finally none, as her generative secretion is used up with age.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book III
claims.quote: A similar condition is the cause of the later sterility of the lioness, for at the first birth she produces five or six, then in the next year four, and again three cubs, then the next number down to one, then none at all

claims.title: Wind-eggs arise without any prior impregnation
claims.statement: Unfertilised wind-eggs are not relics of a previous mating: they arise in hens and geese that have never been impregnated.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book III
claims.quote: Hence some are wont to speak of wind-eggs as not coming into being independently but as mere relics from a previous impregnation. But this is a false view, for sufficient observations have been made of their arising without impregnation in chickens and goslings.

claims.title: Fish lay incomplete eggs because they are too numerous to finish inside
claims.statement: Birds lay their eggs complete, whereas externally spawning fish lay incomplete eggs that finish growing outside the mother, because fish produce too many eggs for all to be completed inside her.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book III
claims.quote: Among creatures that lay eggs externally birds produce their egg perfect, fish imperfect, but the eggs of the latter complete their growth outside as has been said before. The reason is that the fish kind is very fertile; now it is impossible for many eggs to reach completion within the mother and therefore they lay them outside.

claims.title: Bird eggs are two-coloured, all fish eggs one-coloured
claims.statement: The eggs of birds are two-coloured (white and yolk), while the eggs of all fishes are of one colour.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book III
claims.quote: While the eggs of birds are two-coloured, those of all fish are one-coloured.

claims.title: Water birds' eggs have larger, paler yolks than land birds' eggs
claims.statement: Lake (water) birds, being moister and colder than land birds, lay eggs whose yolk is larger and less yellow.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book III
claims.quote: This is what we find in lake birds, for they are of a moister nature and are colder than the land birds, so that the so-called ‘lecithus’ or yolk in the eggs of such birds is large and less yellow because the white is less separated off from it.

claims.title: A hen's egg is laid with the sharp end last
claims.statement: The sharp end of a bird's egg, where it was attached to the uterus, comes out of the hen after the blunt end.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book III
claims.quote: And this is why the sharp end of the egg comes out of the hen later than the blunt end; for the part attached to the uterus comes out later, and the egg is attached at the point where is the said principle, and the principle is in the sharp end.

claims.title: The eggshell is soft when laid and hardens by cooling
claims.statement: A bird's eggshell is still soft when the egg is laid and hardens immediately afterwards by cooling as its moisture evaporates.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book III
claims.quote: it is not observed that the shell is at first only a soft membrane, and that it is only after the egg is perfected that it becomes hard and brittle; this is so nicely adjusted that it is still soft when it comes out (for otherwise it would cause pain in laying), but no sooner has it come out than it is fixed hard by cooling

claims.title: Live-bearing selachians keep the young attached to the uterus by an umbilicus
claims.statement: In some cartilaginous fishes the egg stays attached to the uterus, and when the young fish is complete it is still connected to the uterus by an umbilical cord after the yolk is used up, as in the smooth dogfish.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book III
claims.quote: in some of the cartilaginous fish the egg is not detached from the uterus, but is still connected with it as it comes downwards with a view to the production of the young alive; in these the young fish when perfected is still connected by the umbilicus to the uterus when the egg has been consumed.

claims.title: Fish are prolific because most of their eggs are destroyed
claims.statement: Most fish eggs that are laid are destroyed before hatching, and fish produce great numbers of eggs to make up for this loss.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book III
claims.quote: even as it is most of those laid are destroyed before hatching. Hence the class of fish is prolific, for Nature makes up for the destruction by numbers.

claims.title: All fish have separate sexes except the erythrinus and the channa
claims.statement: In all fishes some individuals have milt organs and others a uterus, except two kinds, the erythrinus and the channa, which have no separate males.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book III
claims.quote: But, as it is, some of them have organs for milt and others have a uterus, and this distinction obtains in all except two, the erythrinus and the channa, some of them having the milt organs, others a uterus.

claims.title: Female fish do not conceive by swallowing milt
claims.statement: Fish are not conceived by the female swallowing the male's milt, because the passage from the mouth leads to the intestine, not the uterus.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book III
claims.quote: as if fish were conceived by the mother’s swallowing the milt,— not considering that this is impossible. For the passage which enters by way of the mouth runs to the intestines, not to the uterus

claims.title: The hyena has only one kind of genitals, not both sexes
claims.statement: The hyena does not have both male and female genitals; each animal has one, but both sexes have a mark under the tail resembling the female genitals.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book III
claims.quote: This is untrue, for the hyena has been seen to have only one pudendum, there being no lack of opportunity for observation in some districts, but hyenas have under the tail a line like the pudendum of the female.

claims.title: Eggs fertilised by one cock take on the nature of a later cock
claims.statement: Eggs already impregnated by one cock change to the nature of a second cock that treads the hen later, provided this happens before the white separates from the yolk.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book III
claims.quote: In birds the wind-eggs become fertile, and those previously impregnated by one kind of cock change their nature to that of the later cock.

claims.title: Insect larvae become motionless, egg-like stages before the adult emerges
claims.statement: Insect larvae, after reaching full size, become a sort of egg: their outer husk hardens and they are motionless, as in bees, wasps and caterpillars.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book III
claims.quote: All these products that are of the nature of a scolex, after progressing and acquiring their full size, become a sort of egg, for the husk about them hardens and they are motionless during this period. This is plain in the scolex of bees and wasps and in caterpillars.

claims.title: Some insects arise spontaneously in wool and water
claims.statement: Some insects come into being without copulation, spontaneously, in wool and similar materials and in water.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book III
claims.quote: Similar to this is also what happens with all other insects which come into being without copulation in wool and other such materials and in water.

claims.title: Worker bees generate drones without copulation
claims.statement: Worker bees produce drones without copulation, being female in generative power but containing both sexes as plants do.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book III
claims.quote: It remains then, as appears to be the case in certain fishes, that the bees should generate the drones without copulation, being indeed female in respect of generative power, but containing in themselves both sexes as plants do.

claims.title: Bee kings generate both kings and workers
claims.statement: The 'kings' (leaders) of a hive generate both their own kind and the worker bees.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book III
claims.quote: since those occupied with the tendance of these creatures deny this, it remains that the kings must generate both their own kind and the bees.

claims.title: Fine seasons bring many drones, rainy seasons many workers
claims.statement: In fine weather bees collect much honey and produce many drones, while in rainy seasons they produce a large brood of ordinary worker bees.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book III
claims.quote: Another fact is also natural, that in fine seasons much honey is collected and many drones are produced but in rainy reasons a large brood of ordinary bees.

claims.title: Observation must take precedence over theory
claims.statement: Where the facts are sufficiently known, credit should be given to observation rather than to theories, and to theories only if they agree with the observed facts.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book III
claims.quote: the facts, however, have not yet been sufficiently grasped; if ever they are, then credit must be given rather to observation than to theories, and to theories only if what they affirm agrees with the observed facts.

claims.title: Few testaceans live on land, many in the sea
claims.statement: Few or no kinds of testaceans (shelled molluscs and the like) live on land, snails being the exception, whereas in the sea there are many of every form.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book III
claims.quote: Because their nature answers to that of plants, therefore few or no kinds of testacea come into being on land, e.g. the snails and any others, few as they are, that resemble them; but in the sea and similar waters there are many of all kinds of forms.

claims.title: Bloodless aquatic animals are rare in fresh water, common in estuaries
claims.statement: Bloodless animals such as testaceans, cephalopods and crustaceans are not found in lakes or in the fresher brackish waters, except exceptionally, but arise in estuaries and at river mouths.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book III
claims.quote: Wherefore animals having no blood and not of a hot nature are not produced in lakes nor in the fresher among brackish waters, but only exceptionally, but it is in estuaries and at the mouths of rivers that they come into being, as testacea and cephalopoda and crustacea

claims.title: Eels and some river fishes arise from scolex-like 'entrails of earth'
claims.statement: Some blooded animals, including a kind of mullet, some other river fishes and the eels, arise without parents in scolex form; eels come into being in the so-called 'entrails of earth'.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book III
claims.quote: even some sanguinea, as a kind of mullet and some other river fishes and also the eel kind. For all of these, though they have but little blood by nature, are nevertheless sanguinea, and have a heart with blood in it as the origin of the parts; and the so-called ‘entrails of earth’, in which comes into being the body of the eel, have the nature of a scolex.

claims.title: All testaceans arise spontaneously from putrefying mud
claims.statement: All testaceans are formed spontaneously, for example on the sides of boats when frothy mud putrefies.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book III
claims.quote: That all the testacea are formed spontaneously is clear from such facts as these. They come into being on the side of boats when the frothy mud putrefies.

claims.title: Male and female twins often lie in the same part of the uterus
claims.statement: Male and female twins are often found together in the same part of the uterus, in all viviparous animals, land animals and fish alike.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book IV
claims.quote: Moreover male and female twins are often found together in the same part of the uterus; this we have observed sufficiently by dissection in all the vivipara, both land animals and fish.

claims.title: Fish and serpents have no testes yet produce both sexes
claims.statement: Fishes and serpents have no testes, yet they produce both male and female offspring, so the testes do not determine sex.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book IV
claims.quote: a proof of this is that many animals in which the distinction of sex exists, and which produce both male and female offspring, nevertheless have no testes, as the footless animals; I mean the classes of fish and of serpents.

claims.title: The male is what can concoct blood into form-bearing semen
claims.statement: The male is defined as the sex able to concoct blood into semen that carries the principle of form; the female receives semen but cannot form or emit it.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book IV
claims.quote: For the male is that which can concoct the blood into semen and which can form and secrete and discharge a semen carrying with it the principle of form

claims.title: Males are hotter than females
claims.statement: Since concoction works by heat and the male concocts semen, the males of animals must be hotter than the females.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book IV
claims.quote: And (2) all concoction works by means of heat. Therefore the males of animals must needs be hotter than the females.

claims.title: An embryo becomes female when the male principle fails for lack of heat
claims.statement: An embryo becomes female when the male principle, through lack of heat, fails to master and concoct the material, which then changes into its opposite.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book IV
claims.quote: For when the first principle does not bear sway and cannot concoct the nourishment through lack of heat nor bring it into its proper form, but is defeated in this respect, then must needs the material which it works on change into its opposite. Now the female is opposite to the male

claims.title: Young and ageing parents produce more females
claims.statement: Parents who are young or approaching old age produce more female offspring than those in their prime.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book IV
claims.quote: For more females are produced by the young and by those verging on old age than by those in the prime of life; in the former the vital heat is not yet perfect, in the latter it is failing.

claims.title: More males are conceived under north winds than south winds
claims.statement: More males are born when copulation takes place while north winds blow than while south winds blow.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book IV
claims.quote: Again, more males are born if copulation takes place when north than when south winds are blowing.

claims.title: Menstruation naturally occurs when the moon is waning
claims.statement: Menstruation naturally occurs more when the month (moon) is waning, that time being colder and moister.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book IV
claims.quote: Also the fact that the catamenia occur in the course of nature rather when the month is waning is due to the same causes.

claims.title: Offspring resemble parents more than remoter ancestors
claims.statement: Children resemble their parents more than their remoter ancestors, and those ancestors more than any chance individual.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book IV
claims.quote: (2) They resemble their parents more than remoter ancestors, and resemble those ancestors more than any chance individual.

claims.title: Unmastered paternal movements revert to those of the grandfather
claims.statement: When the movement from the father in the semen is weakened ('resolved'), it changes into that of his father and then his grandfather, and likewise in the maternal line, so that children may resemble grandparents and remoter ancestors.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book IV
claims.quote: for instance, if the movement of the male parent be resolved, it changes by a very slight difference into that of his father, and in the next instance into that of his grandfather; and in this way not only in the male but also in the female line the movement of the female parent changes into that of her mother

claims.title: Monstrosities are commonest in animals bearing many young, above all fowl
claims.statement: Monstrosities are very rare in animals that bear one young, more frequent in those bearing many, and most frequent in birds, above all the domestic fowl.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book IV
claims.quote: Hence also such monstrosities appear very rarely in animals producing only one young one, more frequently in those producing many, most of all in birds and among birds in the common fowl.

claims.title: Double-yolked eggs with fused yolks yield four-legged, four-winged chicks
claims.statement: In double-yolked eggs, if the yolks are separated by a membrane two normal chicks result, but if the yolks are continuous the chick is monstrous, with one body and head but four legs and four wings.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book IV
claims.quote: when the yolks are continuous, with no division between them, the chickens produced are monstrous, having one body and head but four legs and four wings

claims.title: Hermaphrodite genitals occur in humans and especially in goats
claims.statement: Animals are sometimes born with both male and female genitals; this occurs in humans and especially in goats.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book IV
claims.quote: Again, they may have the generative parts doubled, the one being male, the other female; this is known in men and especially in goats.

claims.title: No animal is born without a heart or wholly without a liver
claims.statement: No animal has ever been born without a heart or entirely without a liver, though animals are born without a spleen, with two spleens or with one kidney.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book IV
claims.quote: No animal, indeed, has ever been born without a heart, but they are born without a spleen or with two spleens or with one kidney; there is no case again of total absence of the liver, but there are cases of its being incomplete.

claims.title: Large animals bear few young, small animals many
claims.statement: Among walking, flying and swimming animals alike, large animals produce few young and small animals many, because in large animals the nutriment goes to increasing the body.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book IV
claims.quote: And not only in animals that walk but also in those that fly or swim the large ones produce few, the small many, for the same reason.

claims.title: Human gestation alone is irregular, seven to ten months
claims.statement: Man alone among animals has an irregular gestation period: children are born from seven to ten months, and eight-month children survive, though less often than the rest.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book IV
claims.quote: On account of this it results that in man alone among animals the period of gestation is irregular; whereas the period is fixed in the rest, there are several periods in man, for children are born at seven months and at ten months and at the times between, for even those of eight months do live though less often than the rest.

claims.title: Women and mares alone accept the male during pregnancy
claims.statement: Women and mares are the only animals that admit the male during gestation.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book IV
claims.quote: therefore women and mares are the only animals which admit the male during gestation

claims.title: Hares superfetate
claims.statement: Superfetation (conceiving a second litter while already pregnant) occurs naturally in hares, because they are small, bear many young and are rich in semen.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book IV
claims.quote: For superfoetation occurs in these animals, since they are not large and they bear many young (for they have many toes and the many-toed animals bear many), and they are spermatic.

claims.title: Hoofed animals bear young complete, most many-toed animals incomplete
claims.statement: Among viviparous animals, solid-hoofed and cloven-footed animals bear their young fully formed, while most many-toed animals bear them imperfect (many born blind).
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book IV
claims.quote: Some of the vivipara produce their young imperfect, others perfect; the one-hoofed and cloven-footed perfect, most of the many-toed imperfect.

claims.title: Young swallows' eyes regrow after being put out
claims.statement: If the eyes of nestling swallows are put out, they recover their sight, because the birds are still developing and the eyes grow afresh.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book IV
claims.quote: Hence if the eyes of swallows while still young be put out they recover their sight again, for the birds are still developing, not yet developed, when the injury is inflicted, so that the eyes grow and sprout afresh.

claims.title: In humans males are more often born defective than females
claims.statement: In man, males are more often born defective than females, but this is not so in other animals.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book IV
claims.quote: In man males are more often born defective than females, but in the other animals this is not the case.

claims.title: Females develop slower in the womb but mature and age faster after birth
claims.statement: In man the female develops more slowly than the male in the womb, but after birth reaches puberty, prime and old age sooner than the male.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book IV
claims.quote: For while within the mother the female takes longer in developing, but after birth everything is perfected more quickly in females than in males; I mean, for instance, puberty, the prime of life, and old age.

claims.title: Nursing women neither menstruate nor conceive
claims.statement: While women are suckling, menstruation naturally does not occur and they do not conceive; if they do conceive, the milk dries up, because milk and menses are the same secretion.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book IV
claims.quote: While women are suckling children the catamenia do not occur according to Nature, nor do they conceive; if they do conceive, the milk dries up.

claims.title: All animals are naturally born head first
claims.statement: The natural birth of all animals is head first, because the parts above the umbilical cord are larger and heavier.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book IV
claims.quote: The natural birth of all animals is head-foremost, because the parts above the umbilical cord are larger than those below.

claims.title: Man lives longer than any animal except the elephant
claims.statement: Man lives longer than any animal for which there is credible evidence, except the elephant.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book IV
claims.quote: Man lives a longer time than any animal of which we have any credible experience except the elephant

claims.title: Gestation length is caused by the size of the offspring, not by lifespan
claims.statement: Gestation length roughly corresponds to lifespan only incidentally; its real cause is the size of the offspring, since large masses take long to perfect.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book IV
claims.quote: but the cause of the time of gestation is the size of the offspring. For it is not easy for large masses to arrive at their perfection in a small time

claims.title: Horses gestate a year, humans ten months, elephants two years
claims.statement: Horses and their kin carry their young for a year, man at most ten months, and elephants for two years.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book IV
claims.quote: That is why horses and animals akin to them, though living a shorter time than man, yet carry their young longer; for the time in the former is a year, but in the latter ten months at the outside. For the same reason also the time is long in elephants; they carry their young two years on account of their excessive size.

claims.title: Eye colour has no final cause unless characteristic of the kind
claims.statement: Features not characteristic of a whole kind, such as an individual's eye colour, do not exist for a final cause but arise of necessity from the material and the efficient cause.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book V
claims.quote: The eye for instance exists for a final cause, but it is not blue for a final cause unless this condition be characteristic of the kind of animal.

claims.title: Embryos sleep most of the time but wake briefly in the womb
claims.statement: Embryos sleep most of the time, though they are found to wake briefly even in the womb, which is why newborns spend most of their time asleep.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book V
claims.quote: But nevertheless they are found to wake even in the womb (this is clear in dissections and in the ovipara), and then they immediately fall into a sleep again. This is why after birth also they spend most of their time in sleep.

claims.title: Infants laugh only in sleep, not awake
claims.statement: Infants do not laugh when awake, but while asleep they both laugh and cry.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book V
claims.quote: When awake infants do not laugh, but while asleep they both laugh and cry.

claims.title: All newborn children have bluish eyes that later change colour
claims.statement: The eyes of all children are bluish at birth and later change to their permanent colour, which is not seen in other animals.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book V
claims.quote: The eyes of all children are bluish immediately after birth; later on they change to the colour which is to be theirs permanently. But in the case of other animals this is not visible.

claims.title: Only horses and humans have eyes of different colours
claims.statement: Of animals other than man, the horse has the greatest variety of eye colour and some horses have two differently coloured eyes; this is seen in no other animal, but sometimes in man.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book V
claims.quote: Of the other animals the horse has the greatest variety of colour in the eye, for some of them are actually heteroglaucous; this phenomenon is not to be seen in any of the other animals, but man is sometimes heteroglaucous.

claims.title: Blue eyes see poorly by day, dark eyes poorly by night
claims.statement: Blue eyes are not keen-sighted by day and dark eyes are not keen-sighted by night.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book V
claims.quote: We must suppose the same cause also to be responsible for the fact that blue eyes are not keen-sighted by day nor dark eyes by night.

claims.title: Cataract attacks blue eyes more, night-blindness dark eyes
claims.statement: Cataract affects blue-eyed people more, while nyctalopia affects dark-eyed people more.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book V
claims.quote: Cataract attacks the blue-eyed more, but what is called ‘nyctalopia’ the dark-eyed.

claims.title: Animals with deep-set eyes see far, those with prominent eyes do not
claims.statement: Animals with prominent eyes do not see well at a distance, whereas those whose eyes lie deep in the head can see distant things.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book V
claims.quote: A proof of this is that animals with prominent eyes do not see well at a distance, whereas those which have their eyes lying deep in the head can see things at a distance

claims.title: The seal has no external ears, only hearing passages
claims.statement: The seal, though a viviparous quadruped, has no external ears but only passages for hearing, because it lives in the water.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book V
claims.quote: The workmanship of Nature is admirable also in the seal, for though a viviparous quadruped it has no ears but only passages for hearing. This is because its life is passed in the water

claims.title: Only humans visibly go grey with age, and to a lesser degree horses
claims.statement: Humans go grey on the head as they age, but this is not visible in practically any other animal except, to some extent, the horse.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book V
claims.quote: Human beings also go grey on the head as they grow old, but this is not visible in practically any other animal, though more so in the horse than others.

claims.title: Men go bald in front and grey first at the temples
claims.statement: Men go bald on the front of the head but turn grey first on the temples; no one goes bald first on the temples or the back of the head.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book V
claims.quote: Men go bald on the front of the head, but turn grey first on the temples; no one goes bald first on these or on the back of the head.

claims.title: Peoples of moist cold lands are straight-haired, of hot dry lands curly
claims.statement: Peoples living in moist air, such as the Scythians and Thracians, are straight-haired, while Ethiopians and others in hot countries are curly-haired because their brains and the surrounding air are dry.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book V
claims.quote: For this reason the Scythians on the Black Sea and the Thracians are straight-haired, for both they themselves and the environing air are moist, whereas the Aethiopians and men in hot countries are curly-haired, for their brains and the surrounding air are dry.

claims.title: Deep-water sea-urchins have large, hard spines because of cold
claims.statement: Sea-urchins that live in deep, cold water (sixty fathoms or more) have large, hard spines though their bodies are small.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book V
claims.quote: For these, too, though small themselves, have large and hard spines because the sea in which they live is cold on account of its depth (for they are found in sixty fathoms and even more).

claims.title: Women and eunuchs do not go bald
claims.statement: Women do not go bald, since like children they produce no seminal secretion, and eunuchs do not go bald because they change into the female condition.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book V
claims.quote: Women do not go bald because their nature is like that of children, both alike being incapable of producing seminal secretion. Eunuchs do not become bald, because they change into the female condition.

claims.title: Hair covered by hats goes grey sooner
claims.statement: Greying is a kind of decay, so hair protected by hats or other coverings, being sheltered from the winds, goes grey sooner.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book V
claims.quote: hair protected by hats or other coverings goes grey sooner (for the winds prevent decay and the protection keeps off the winds)

claims.title: White individuals occur in normally uniform-coloured species
claims.statement: Even in uniformly coloured kinds, white individuals occasionally arise when development is perverted, as has been seen in partridges, ravens, sparrows and bears.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book V
claims.quote: but still they do so change, for before now white individuals have been observed among partridges, ravens, sparrows, and bears.

claims.title: Hot drinking water whitens hair, cold water darkens it
claims.statement: Colour change in animals whose kind is many-coloured is due to the water they drink: hot waters make the hair white and cold waters make it dark.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book V
claims.quote: This is owing to the water which they drink, for hot waters make the hair white, cold makes it dark, an effect found also in plants.

claims.title: The belly is whiter in animals that are not uniformly coloured
claims.statement: In all animals that are not uniformly coloured, the underside of the belly is whiter.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book V
claims.quote: Hence also in all animals not uniformly coloured all the part under the belly is whiter.

claims.title: Females have higher voices than males, except in cattle
claims.statement: In animals generally the female's voice is higher than the male's, most plainly in man, but in cattle the cow's voice is deeper than the bull's.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book V
claims.quote: in the other kinds of animals the voice of the female is higher than that of the male (this being especially plain in man, for Nature has given this faculty to him in the highest degree because he alone of animals makes use of speech and the voice is the material of speech), but in cattle the opposite obtains, for the voice of cows is deeper than that of bulls.

claims.title: A bone is found in the heart of some bulls
claims.statement: A bone is found in the heart of some bulls.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book V
claims.quote: That the heart of bulls is of such a nature is shown by the fact that a bone is actually found in some of them

claims.title: Castrated animals take on a female voice and character
claims.statement: All animals, when castrated, change to the female character and utter a voice like that of females.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book V
claims.quote: All animals when castrated change to the female character, and utter a voice like that of the females because the sinewy strength in the principle of the voice is relaxed.

claims.title: The pig does not shed its teeth; lions shed only their canines
claims.statement: The pig does not shed its teeth, and some carnivores, such as lions, shed no teeth except the canines.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book V
claims.quote: Yet the pig also suckles but does not shed its teeth, and, further, all the animals with carnivorous dentition suckle, but some of them do not shed any teeth except the canines, e.g. lions.

claims.title: Nature never fails nor does anything in vain
claims.statement: Nature never fails nor does anything in vain, so far as is possible in each case.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book V
claims.quote: Now we assume, basing our assumption upon what we see, that Nature never fails nor does anything in vain so far as is possible in each case.

claims.title: Young fed hotter milk cut their teeth sooner
claims.statement: Suckling itself does not form the teeth, but the heat of the milk speeds them: young that receive hotter milk grow their teeth more quickly.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book V
claims.quote: A proof of this is that even in suckling animals those young which enjoy hotter milk grow their teeth quicker, heat being conducive to growth.

claims.title: The last human grinders erupt around age twenty
claims.statement: The grinding teeth keep growing for a long time, the last of them cutting the gum at about twenty years of age and sometimes in old age.
claims.author: Aristotle
claims.chapter: On the Generation of Animals, Book V
claims.quote: A proof of this is that even the flat teeth grow for a long time, the last of them cutting the gum at about twenty years of age; indeed in some cases the last teeth have been grown in quite old age.

claims.title: Fisher's fundamental theorem of natural selection (partial-change form)
claims.statement: The rate of increase in mean fitness of a population due to natural selection equals its additive genetic variance in fitness at that time.
claims.author: Ronald A. Fisher
claims.work: The Genetical Theory of Natural Selection
claims.chapter: The Genetical Theory of Natural Selection (1930)

claims.title: Fisher-KPP wave of advance of an advantageous gene
claims.statement: An advantageous allele spreading through a continuous population advances as a travelling wave whose speed is set by the selection coefficient and the diffusion (dispersal) rate.
claims.author: Ronald A. Fisher
claims.work: The wave of advance of advantageous genes
claims.chapter: The wave of advance of advantageous genes (1937)

claims.title: Fisher's principle of equal investment in the sexes
claims.statement: Under random mating and autosomal inheritance, selection drives parents to invest equally in sons and daughters, which gives a 1:1 sex ratio when the two cost the same.
claims.author: Ronald A. Fisher
claims.work: The Genetical Theory of Natural Selection
claims.chapter: The Genetical Theory of Natural Selection (1930)

claims.title: Fisher's infinitesimal model of quantitative inheritance
claims.statement: Continuous traits determined by many Mendelian loci of small additive effect produce the observed correlations between relatives, so biometric and Mendelian inheritance are consistent.
claims.author: Ronald A. Fisher
claims.work: The Correlation between Relatives on the Supposition of Mendelian Inheritance
claims.chapter: The Correlation between Relatives on the Supposition of Mendelian Inheritance (1919)

claims.title: Turing diffusion-driven instability
claims.statement: A homogeneous steady state of two reacting chemicals that is stable without diffusion can become unstable to spatial perturbations when the chemicals diffuse at different rates, spontaneously producing a pattern.
claims.author: Alan Turing
claims.chapter: The chemical basis of morphogenesis (1952)

claims.title: Turing wavelength selection
claims.statement: The spacing of a Turing pattern at onset is set by the reaction rates and diffusivities, not by the size of the tissue, so changing these parameters predictably changes the number of repeated elements.
claims.author: Alan Turing
claims.chapter: The chemical basis of morphogenesis (1952)

claims.title: Reaction-diffusion of morphogens accounts for biological pattern
claims.statement: Chemical substances that react and diffuse through tissue (morphogens) are sufficient to account for the main phenomena of morphogenesis.
claims.author: Alan Turing
claims.chapter: The chemical basis of morphogenesis (1952)

claims.title: Kimura fixation probability of a mutant allele
claims.statement: The probability that a mutant allele eventually fixes in a finite population depends on its initial frequency, its selective advantage and the effective population size, and equals its initial frequency when it is neutral.
claims.author: Motoo Kimura
claims.work: On the probability of fixation of mutant genes in a population
claims.chapter: On the probability of fixation of mutant genes in a population (1962)

claims.title: Neutral substitution rate equals the mutation rate
claims.statement: For neutral mutations the long-run rate of molecular substitution equals the mutation rate per generation, independent of population size, which yields a molecular clock.
claims.author: Motoo Kimura
claims.work: Evolutionary Rate at the Molecular Level
claims.chapter: Evolutionary Rate at the Molecular Level (1968)

claims.title: Mean time to fixation of a neutral mutant
claims.statement: A neutral mutant that does go to fixation takes on average about four times the effective population size, in generations, to do so.
claims.author: Motoo Kimura
claims.work: The average number of generations until fixation of a mutant gene in a finite population
claims.chapter: The average number of generations until fixation of a mutant gene in a finite population (1969)

claims.title: Neutral equilibrium heterozygosity (Kimura-Crow)
claims.statement: Under neutral mutation to new alleles and drift, expected heterozygosity reaches an equilibrium that rises with the product of effective population size and mutation rate.
claims.author: Motoo Kimura
claims.work: The number of alleles that can be maintained in a finite population
claims.chapter: The number of alleles that can be maintained in a finite population (1964)

claims.title: Neutral theory: most molecular substitutions are neutral
claims.statement: Most evolutionary changes at the molecular level are caused by random drift of selectively neutral or nearly neutral mutations, not by positive selection.
claims.author: Motoo Kimura
claims.work: Evolutionary Rate at the Molecular Level
claims.chapter: Evolutionary Rate at the Molecular Level (1968)

claims.title: Hamilton's rule
claims.statement: A gene for social behaviour increases in frequency when the benefit to the recipient, weighted by genetic relatedness, exceeds the cost to the actor.
claims.author: W. D. Hamilton
claims.work: The genetical evolution of social behaviour. I
claims.chapter: The genetical evolution of social behaviour. I (1964)

claims.title: Haplodiploidy hypothesis for eusociality
claims.statement: Because full sisters in haplodiploid species share three quarters of their genes, more than a mother shares with her offspring, haplodiploid insects are predisposed to evolve sterile worker castes.
claims.author: W. D. Hamilton
claims.work: The genetical evolution of social behaviour. II
claims.chapter: The genetical evolution of social behaviour. II (1964)

claims.title: Local mate competition sex ratio
claims.statement: When a few mothers lay eggs on a patch and their offspring mate there before the daughters disperse, the evolutionarily stable sex ratio is female-biased, and the bias weakens as the number of mothers grows.
claims.author: W. D. Hamilton
claims.chapter: Extraordinary Sex Ratios (1967)

claims.title: Declining force of selection with age
claims.statement: The strength of selection on survival falls with age after reproduction begins, so senescence is an inevitable outcome of natural selection.
claims.author: W. D. Hamilton
claims.work: The moulding of senescence by natural selection
claims.chapter: The moulding of senescence by natural selection (1966)

claims.title: Evolutionarily stable strategy conditions
claims.statement: A strategy is evolutionarily stable if, once common, it cannot be invaded by any rare alternative strategy.
claims.author: John Maynard Smith
claims.chapter: The Logic of Animal Conflict (1973)

claims.title: Hawk-Dove mixed ESS
claims.statement: When the cost of injury exceeds the value of the contested resource, the stable outcome is a mixture in which animals escalate with probability equal to the ratio of resource value to injury cost.
claims.author: John Maynard Smith
claims.work: Evolution and the Theory of Games
claims.chapter: Evolution and the Theory of Games (1982)

claims.title: War of attrition ESS
claims.statement: In contests settled by display, where the animal willing to persist longer wins and costs grow with time, the stable strategy is to choose a persistence time at random from an exponential distribution whose mean equals the resource value.
claims.author: John Maynard Smith
claims.work: The theory of games and the evolution of animal conflicts
claims.chapter: The theory of games and the evolution of animal conflicts (1974)

claims.title: Twofold cost of sex
claims.statement: An asexual mutant female in a sexual population with equal sex ratio produces twice as many grandchildren as a sexual female, so sex needs a compensating advantage of up to twofold to persist.
claims.author: John Maynard Smith
claims.chapter: The Evolution of Sex (1978)

claims.title: Genetic hitchhiking (selective sweep)
claims.statement: When a favourable mutation sweeps to fixation, it reduces genetic variation at closely linked neutral sites, and the reduction is larger the tighter the linkage relative to the strength of selection.
claims.author: John Maynard Smith
claims.work: The hitch-hiking effect of a favourable gene
claims.chapter: The hitch-hiking effect of a favourable gene (1974)
